            FORCE MAJEURE
12.1 Notice of FME. A Party claiming impact by an FME must provide written notice to the other Party as early
as commercially practicable, but in no event later than 10 Business Days after the initial occurrence of the FME.
In the written notice, the affected Party must describe the nature and, if known, cause of the FME, the estimated
duration of the FME, the anticipated effect of the FME on the ability of the Party to perform its obligations or satisfy
any condition under this PPA (including, if occurring after COA and Generator is the affected Party, information
reasonably required to determine the amount of Force Majeure Energy), and any actions that have or will be taken
to avoid or minimize the effect of the FME. The affected Party must deliver to the other Party regular updated
reports and any additional documentation and analysis supporting its claim regarding an ongoing FME. When the
affected Party can resume performance of its obligations under this PPA, the affected Party must promptly provide
written notice to the other Party and promptly resume the performance. If determined by GPC to be necessary,
Generator must also provide a written certification from a Professional Engineer reasonably acceptable to GPC
that the FME was cured. Despite the preceding sentences, if the affected Party fails to provide initial written notice
within the 10 Business Days or, after the affected Party’s initial notice, the affected Party fails to provide reasonable
reports and substantiation of the claimed FME as required by this Part 12 (Force Majeure), the event or condition
will be deemed not to be an FME and the affected Party’s performance will not be excused as a result of an FME.
12.2 Duty to Mitigate. A Party claiming impact by a FME must: (i) continue to perform its obligations under this
PPA to the extent not affected by the FME; (ii) use reasonable efforts to mitigate the effect of the FME as soon as
reasonably practicable; and (iii) remedy its inability to perform as soon as reasonably practicable, but this Section
12.2 (Duty to Mitigate) will not require the settlement of any non-site specific strike, walkout, lockout, or other
general labor dispute on terms which, in the sole judgment of the affected Party, are contrary to its interest.
12.3 Excused Performance; Substantiation; Extension of RMCD. If an FME occurs, subject to compliance
with all Sections of this Part 12 (Force Majeure), the affected Party will be excused from performance of its
obligations impacted by the FME, other than payment obligations that accrued before the declaration of the FME,
and will not be construed to be in default in respect of the obligations to the extent that, and for so long as, failure
to perform is due to an FME. However, the suspension of performance due to an FME will be of no greater scope
and of no longer duration than is required by the FME. Despite any other provision in this PPA, no FME will extend
this PPA beyond the Term.
         12.3.1. Burden of Proof and Supporting Documentation. The burden of proof regarding whether an
         FME occurred and the impact of an FME will be upon the affected Party. If the affected Party requests
         that its performance be excused because of an FME, then the affected Party must support its request with
         documentation demonstrating: (i) the existence of an FME; (ii) efforts by the affected Party to overcome
         or mitigate the effect of the FME; and (iii) after the conclusion of the FME, an analysis of the number of
         Days the FME delayed or otherwise prevented the performance of the affected Party’s obligations or
         satisfaction of any PPA condition and, if the FME occurred after COA, the proposed methodology for
         calculating Force Majeure Energy. The affected Party must provide required documentation by no later
         than five Business Days after the date the FME concludes.
         12.3.2. Extension of RMCD. If an FME directly impacts the critical path of the activities shown on
         Generator’s Milestone Schedule in a manner that prevents Generator from achieving Mechanical

         be delayed because of the critical path delay, so long as, as a condition to any extension of the RMCD,
         Generator complied with all applicable conditions of this Part 12 (Force Majeure), including Generator
         undertaking all commercially reasonable efforts to avoid, overcome, or otherwise mitigate the delay by
         revising, rearranging, expediting, and accelerating the Milestone Schedule.
12.4 Extended FME.
         12.4.1. Notice and Remedy Plan for Extended FME. If the affected Party has reason to believe that a
         suspension of performance due to an FME will continue for a period of six months or longer after the initial
         suspension of performance resulting from the FME (“Extended FME”), the affected Party must notify the
         other Party promptly and submit an FME Remedy Plan to the other Party within 30 Days after the affected
         Party’s initial notice to the other Party. In addition, if the other Party has reason to believe that an FME will
         be an Extended FME, the other Party may request that the affected Party submit an FME Remedy Plan,
         which the affected Party must submit to the requesting Party within 30 Days of the request. An FME
         Remedy Plan must set forth a plan and schedule for mitigation and other remedial measures (including
         necessary repairs, improvements, and changes to operations, as applicable) to cure the effects of the
         FME to enable the affected Party to resume full performance of the suspended obligations under this PPA
         as soon as reasonably practicable.
         12.4.2. Monthly Status Reports and Updates to FME Remedy Plan. While an FME Remedy Plan is in
         effect, the affected Party must provide monthly status reports to the other Party regarding the
         implementation of the FME Remedy Plan, any other measures to remedy the FME, any changes to the
         FME Remedy Plan, and the expected remaining duration of the suspended performance and must provide
         any additional relevant information as may be reasonably requested by the other Party. The affected Party
         must modify the FME Remedy Plan if and as needed to achieve the objective of resuming full performance
         of the suspended obligations under this PPA as soon as reasonably practicable.
         12.4.3. Early Termination Resulting from an Extended FME. If Generator remains unable to perform
         its PPA obligations for more than six months after the initial suspension of performance due to the FME,
         GPC may terminate this PPA effective upon 10 Days’ prior written notice to Generator.
         12.4.4. Liability Following Termination. Upon any termination of this PPA as provided in Section 12.4.3
         (Early Termination Resulting from an Extended FME), the Parties shall have no further liability or obligation
         to each other except for any obligation arising before the date of the termination or as provided in Section
         14.13 (Survival of Rights). Upon termination of this PPA in accordance with Section 12.4.3, Generator will
         not be liable for Termination Liquidated Damages so long as Generator has complied with the
         requirements of this Section 12.4 (Extended FME).

            PPA AMENDMENT; ASSIGNMENT; GENERATOR NAME CHANGE; CHANGE OF CONTROL
13.1 Amendments. This PPA may be amended only by a written instrument duly executed by both Parties,
each of which has received, if applicable, all approvals of governmental authorities of competent jurisdiction
necessary for the effectiveness of this PPA. In recognition of GPC’s administrative burden resulting from multiple
amendments requested by Generator, and subject to Section 13.2.3 (Reimbursement of GPC’s Costs), Generator
agrees that each amendment requested by Generator after the first amendment will be subject to the payment by
Generator to GPC of a fee of $2,500, which Generator must pay to GPC before GPC’s execution of the
amendment.
13.2 PPA Assignment. Except as expressly provided in Section 13.4 (Financing Assignment), Generator must
not assign this PPA or its rights or obligations, in whole or in part, to any person or entity except with GPC’s prior
written consent, and the proposed assignee (proposed new Generator) must: (i) agree to assume Generator’s
PPA obligations; (ii) deliver, on GPC’s reasonable request, assurance of its creditworthiness and its ability to
perform all PPA obligations; and (iii) cooperate to comply with any applicable law. In addition, Generator and the
proposed assignee must comply with Section 13.2.1 (Request for Consent) through Section 13.2.5 (New Account
with GPC) of this Section 13.2 (PPA Assignment) as conditions precedent to the effectiveness of any PPA
assignment. If Generator or the proposed assignee fails to comply with any of this Section 13.2 (PPA Assignment),
the attempted assignment of this PPA will be void (except for a collateral assignment under Section 13.4
(Financing Assignment)). Any assignment of this PPA authorized under this Section 13.2 (PPA Assignment) will
constitute, as of the effective date of the assignment, an acceptance and assumption by the assignee (new
Generator) of all Generator PPA obligations and a release and discharge by GPC of the assignor from the
obligations arising after the effective date of the assignment.

so long as: (i) Generator provides written notice to GPC in advance; and (ii) the transaction does not: (a) limit

(c) release or discharge Generator from any PPA obligation or liability; or (d) require substitution or amendment
of payment security, insurance, W-9, customer account number, or billing address. A Change of Control
transaction that requires substitution or amendment of payment security, insurance, W-9, customer account
number, or billing address will be documented and treated as if it were an Assignment and Section 13.2 (PPA
Assignment) will apply. GPC may lower the fee charged for a Change of Control transaction if Generator’s request
meets the requirements of Section 13.6 (Multiple Requests for Assignment or Change of Control).

14.4 Contract Interpretation. Each exhibit, attachment, appendix, schedule, regulatory requirement, policy,
procedure, standard, or other document attached to or referenced in this PPA (expressly including the Schedule
of Defined Terms) is incorporated into, and is integral to, this PPA as if included in the main body. In this PPA and
in all attached or incorporated documents: (i) whenever the term “include,” “including,” or “e.g.” is used in
connection with a listing of items included within or an example of the prior reference, the listing will be interpreted
to be illustrative only, and will not be interpreted as a limitation on or exclusive listing of the items included in the
prior reference; and (ii) “or” means either or all (i.e., “A or B” means “A or B or both A and B”).
Unless otherwise specified, a reference to a given agreement or document, and all the schedules, exhibits,
appendices, and attachments to the agreement or document, will be a reference to that agreement or document
as modified, amended, supplemented, or restated, and in effect from time to time. Whenever the term “consent”
or “approval” is used, the consent or approval will not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed by the
consenting or approving Party, unless this PPA provides that the consent or approval is in the sole discretion of
the consenting Party. If the Party has provided email contact information, “written” or “in writing” includes email
communication, absent express statement otherwise.
Reference to: (i) a Party or Person includes any allowed successor or assign; (ii) a regulatory authority includes
an authority succeeding to the same function; and (iii) an applicable law is to the law as modified or amended and
then effective. Reference to a PPA part by caption (e.g., Facility Operations) or number (e.g., Part 6 (Facility
Operations)) includes all separate sections (e.g., Section 6.3 (Annual Delivered Energy) and clauses (e.g., 6.3.1
(Maximum Energy Contract Amount)) within that part and reference to a section by caption or number includes all
separate clauses within that section.
A defined term may be singular or plural, as the context requires, and, absent an express statement otherwise,
each defined term has the same meaning in all PPA documents. Captions are for convenience only and do not
affect PPA interpretation. GPC will calculate all dollar per kW references in this PPA based on the Facility Size
(AC), except when Exhibit A (Project Information) states an Interconnection Limit. If Exhibit A (Project Information)
states an Interconnection Limit, then GPC will calculate all dollar per kW references based on Interconnection
Limit.

In accordance with PPA Section 7.3 (Performance Security), a Generator that is not Creditworthy must deliver
to GPC Performance Security. GPC will determine whether Generator is Creditworthy and will reflect its
determination by checking the applicable box above.

    1. Performance Security Amount and Timing. The required Performance Security amounts are
       calculated by multiplying Facility size (kW), or, if applicable, Interconnection Limit, by the applicable
       rate in the Performance Security Table. The applicable rate is the rate ($/kW) that corresponds to the
       Term length and the relevant time period (e.g., before or after the Initial Synchronization Request
       date).

             A. Initial Performance Security. By no later than five Business Days after the Execution Date,
                Generator must post Eligible Collateral in the Performance Security amount required by the
                first $/kW row of the Performance Security Table below. Generator must maintain
                Performance Security required by this Section 1.A (Initial Performance Security) until initial
                Performance Security is increased or replaced under Section 1.B (Increased Performance
                Security).

             B. Increased Performance Security. After the Initial Synchronization Request date, Generator
                must maintain Eligible Collateral in the Performance Security amount required by the second
                $/kW row of the Performance Security Table. By no later than the Initial Synchronization
                Request date, Generator must either (i) increase its Eligible Collateral value to the
                Performance Security amount; or (ii) provide replacement Eligible Collateral in a value equal
                to the Performance Security amount.

    2. Pre-Approval of Eligible Collateral. By no later than the date Generator returns the partially
       executed PPA and IA to GPC, Generator must: (i) notify GPC of the Eligible Collateral form Generator
       intends to provide to meet its initial Performance Security obligation; and (ii) provide a draft Letter of
       Credit or Generator Guaranty to GPC for review and approval if Generator intends to post a Letter of
       Credit or Generator Guaranty as Eligible Collateral. By no later than three weeks before the Initial
       Synchronization Request, Generator must: (a) notify GPC of Generator’s election under Section 1.B
       to either increase its Eligible Collateral value or replace its Eligible Collateral; and (b) provide a draft
       Letter of Credit or Generator Guaranty if Generator intends to amend or replace Eligible Collateral in
       the form of a Letter of Credit or Generator Guaranty.

    3. Impact of Delay Damages. If Generator posted Performance Security and subsequently accrues
       Delay Damages under PPA Section 5.2 (Failure to Submit the Initial Synchronization Request by the
       Required Notice Date for Initial Synchronization), GPC may draw upon Performance Security for the
       Delay Damages due, and Generator must replenish or replace the Performance Security by no later
       than three Business Days after GPC’s notice of its draw upon the Performance Security.

    4. Impact of Unused Delay Damages Performance Security. This Section 4 (Impact of Unused Delay
       Damages Performance Security) is applicable if: Generator is not Creditworthy and was required to
       post Delay Damages Performance Security.

       If Generator fails to comply with the preceding sentence, GPC will be entitled, without limitation to its
       other remedies under the PPA or at law, to draw the full amount of the existing Performance Security
       before the expiration date of the Performance Security.

    6. Draws and Replenishment of Performance Security. In addition to draws permitted by Section 3
       (Impact of Delay Damages) of this Exhibit B (Performance Security), GPC may draw upon
       Performance Security to recover any damages arising from a Generator PPA breach or other amounts
       due and owing to GPC under the PPA, including Termination Liquidated Damages owed under PPA
       Section 9.2.2 (Termination Damages). In the event of a draw on the Performance Security, then,
       unless GPC has exercised its right to terminate the PPA under PPA Section 9.2 (Termination for
       Default; Termination for Damages; No-Fault Termination), Generator must replenish Performance
       Security to the full amount required by this Exhibit B (Performance Security) within three Business
       Days after GPC notifies Generator of GPC’s draw upon the Performance Security.

    7. Change to Form of Eligible Collateral held as Performance Security. Generator may request to
       replace the form of its Eligible Collateral at any time during the Term; however, in order to compensate
       GPC for the resources expended in assisting Generator with the replacement process (i.e., review
       and approval of replacement Eligible Collateral, processing of Eligible Collateral swap, participating
       in financial closing activities, etc.), a fee of $2,500 per occurrence will be charged to Generator.

       part of a PPA assignment or Change of Control, Generator will not be required to pay the $2,500 fee
       to replace Generator’s Eligible Collateral form if Generator pays the fee for an Assignment or Change
       of Control required by Section 13.2 (PPA Assignment), Section 13.5 (Change of Control), or Section
       13.6 (Multiple Requests for Assignment or Change of Control).

    8. Creditworthy Status. If a Creditworthy Generator loses its Creditworthy status during the Term,

          Guarantor will derive substantial direct and indirect benefit from the transactions contemplated by the PPA.

PART 1 DEFINITIONS
1.1 Definitions. Unless otherwise defined in this Guaranty, capitalized terms have the meanings specified
or referred to in the PPA.

PART 2 GUARANTY
2.1 Guaranty. Guarantor unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees to Beneficiary and Beneficiary’s
successors and assigns, that Guarantor will make prompt and full payment of any obligations of Company to
Beneficiary when due, whether by acceleration or otherwise, with any interest as may accrue under the PPA
or under any other documents or instruments now or in the future evidencing, securing, or otherwise relating to
the PPA (“Guaranteed Obligations”), except that Guarantor’s liability under this Guaranty will in no event
exceed the aggregate amount of Eligible Collateral that Company must provide in accordance with PPA Exhibit
C (Performance Security) (plus costs of enforcement of this Guaranty as provided in Section 4.4 (Expenses)).
Guarantor must immediately pay for any obligation of Company upon demand by Beneficiary.

   Person, and Guarantor is the principal obligor under this Guaranty. Guarantor’s liability under this Guaranty
   will be direct and immediate and not conditional or contingent upon the pursuit of any remedies against
   Company or any other person, nor against securities or liens available to Beneficiary or Beneficiary’s

===== DKT 56765 FCR-27 STF-JKA-1-PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/STF-JKA-1-45.docx =====
STF-JKA-1-45

Question: 

Since FCR 26, the Company filed 6 monthly IFR notification reports since the under-recovered fuel balance exceeded 200 million dollars in each of those months. In each case, the Company did not propose an adjustment. After the first report was filed on May 14, 2025, which indicated that the fuel balance exceeded the $200 million threshold in April 2025, the under-recovered fuel balance continued to increase for another 3 months. Under what circumstances would the Company decide to propose an interim fuel rate increase or a fuel rate decrease?

Response:

On a case-by-case basis, the Company would consider a variety of factors including the latest natural gas and other fuel price forecasts, observed volatility of fuel markets, and the relative projected fuel over or under-recovery balances through the current test period. Other factors may include the historical trend of fuel over or under-recovery balances and the proximity to the next fuel case proceeding.

            TERM OF AGREEMENT
2.1     Term. This PPA will become effective on the date on which GPC signs this PPA, as shown on the signature
page, and, subject to any earlier termination under the terms of this PPA, will remain in full effect through, and will
expire upon the completion of, 10 Annual Periods.
2.2     Survival. All provisions of this PPA that expressly or by implication come into or continue in effect following
the expiration or termination of this PPA will remain in effect and be enforceable following the expiration or
termination.
2.3    Conditions to Performance. Performance of this PPA is subject to the Commission awarding a
Commission Certificate, and if required by Legal Requirements, FERC issuing an order accepting this PPA, in
each case as provided below:
         2.3.1. FERC Acceptance. If FERC acceptance of this PPA is required by Legal Requirements, and if
         (i) FERC issues a valid order rejecting this PPA, or (ii) FERC takes action that has the effect of delaying
         the date when FERC will issue an order accepting this PPA to a date beyond 285 Days after the granting
         of a Commission Certificate, then the Parties will meet within 10 Business Days after the order or action
         to negotiate amendments to this PPA that extend the time for FERC to accept the PPA beyond 285 Days
         after the granting of a Commission Certificate, or other appropriate measures, so that this PPA is legal
         and fully enforceable without materially increasing the risks for either Party or adversely affecting the value
         of the economic bargain to either Party contemplated by this PPA in its original form. If the Parties are
         unable to negotiate any acceptable amendments, or other appropriate measures, either Party may
         terminate this PPA upon written notice to the other Party, provided that such notice is delivered to the non-
         terminating Party no later than 30 Days after 285 Days from the granting of a Commission Certificate.
         This termination right will not be available to the Parties, and the Parties will be deemed to have waived
         such termination right, absent receipt of the notice by the non-terminating Party before the expiration of
         the 30-Day period.
         Notwithstanding the foregoing, if, prior to 285 Days after the granting of a Commission Certificate, FERC
         issues a valid order accepting this PPA subject to material modifications or conditions, including
         acceptance subject to refund following an administrative proceeding, the adversely-affected Party or
         Parties will have the right to terminate this PPA if such material modifications or conditions are not
         acceptable to such Party or Parties. Within 15 Days after the issuance of a FERC order, Generator must
         provide GPC with a copy of the FERC order along with written notice of whether the FERC order is subject
         to material modifications or conditions that adversely affect Generator and, if so, whether the material
         modifications or conditions are acceptable to Generator. If Generator fails to provide such written notice
         within such 15-Day period, any FERC order accepting this PPA subject to material modifications or
         conditions will be deemed to be acceptable to Generator. Within 15 Days after receipt of a copy of the
         FERC order from Generator, GPC must provide Generator with written notice of whether the FERC order
         is subject to material modifications or conditions that adversely affect GPC and, if so, whether the material
         modifications or conditions are acceptable to GPC. If GPC fails to provide such notice within such 15-Day
         period, any FERC order accepting this PPA subject to material modifications or conditions will be deemed
         to be acceptable to GPC.
         If either Party provides written notice that the material modifications are not acceptable, the Parties will
         meet within 10 Business Days after the notice to negotiate amendments to this PPA, or other appropriate
         measures, so that this PPA is legal and fully enforceable without materially increasing the risks for either
         Party or adversely affecting the value of the economic bargain to either Party contemplated by this PPA
         in its original form. If the Parties are unable to negotiate any acceptable amendments, or other appropriate
         measures, the Party who delivers the notice will have the right to terminate this PPA upon written notice
         to the other Party if the written notice is delivered no later than 30 Days after 285 Days following the
         granting of a Commission Certificate. Upon a termination under this Section 2.3.1 (FERC Acceptance),
         neither Party will have any liability to the other Party under this PPA.

         2.3.2. Commission Certificate. If, after 250 Days following the filing date by GPC of the application
         with the Commission for a Commission Certificate (“Commission Certificate Target Date”), (i) the
         Commission has not approved this PPA and denied granting a Commission Certificate, or (ii) the
         Commission has issued a Commission Certificate that is subject to material qualifications or conditions
         that adversely affect GPC, GPC may terminate this PPA upon written notice to Generator, so long as such
         notice is delivered to Generator no later than 30 Days after the Commission Certificate Target Date. If
         within 30 Days after the Commission Certificate Target Date the issuance or denial of the Commission
         Certificate has been appealed to the Commission or Fulton County Superior Court, GPC may terminate
         this PPA upon written notice to Generator, so long as such notice is delivered to Generator no later than
         80 Days after the Commission Certificate Target Date. If GPC fails to exercise the above termination right
         within the applicable notice period, GPC will be deemed to have waived such termination right.
         Notwithstanding the foregoing, if at any time the Commission amends the Commission Certificate
         regarding this PPA (“Amended Commission Certificate”) and the Amended Commission Certificate
         imposes material qualifications or conditions that adversely affect GPC, unless GPC and Generator agree
         to amend under Section 2.3.3 (Commission Modification/Amendment), GPC will have a unilateral right to
         terminate this PPA if the material qualifications or conditions are not acceptable to GPC. Within 15 Days
         after the issuance of the Amended Commission Certificate, GPC must provide Generator with written
         notice of whether the Amended Commission Certificate is subject to material qualifications or conditions
         and, if so, whether the material qualifications or conditions are acceptable to GPC. If GPC fails to provide
         such notice within the 15-Day period, the Amended Commission Certificate will be deemed to be
         acceptable to GPC. Upon termination of this PPA under this Section 2.3.2, neither Party will have any
         further liability to the other Party under this PPA. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this PPA, and
         if it is not otherwise required by Commission Rule 515-3-4.08, neither Party will seek to have the
         Commission revoke the Commission Certificate of its own initiative for reasons solely related to changed
         economic circumstances or market conditions affecting this PPA.
         2.3.3. Commission Modification/Amendment. If the Commission issues an order approving this PPA
         with any modification or condition, or issues an Amended Commission Certificate, as applicable, this PPA
         will not be amended to include the modification or condition unless the Parties execute a written
         amendment agreeing to any modification or condition. If GPC requests, within 30 Days after the issuance
         of the order, that Generator execute a written amendment agreeing to the modifications or conditions and
         Generator does not execute the written amendment within 30 Days after the request, GPC may terminate
         this PPA. Upon termination of this PPA under this Section 2.3.3, GPC must promptly return any unused
         portion of the Performance Security to Generator and, afterwards, neither Party will have any further
         obligation to the other Party in this PPA.

         provisions of this PPA in accordance with the intent of the Parties to minimize Taxes so long as neither
         Party is materially adversely affected by such efforts.
         4.3.4. Deductions. If Generator is required by Legal Requirements to remit or pay Taxes that are GPC’s
         responsibility in this PPA, Generator may include such Taxes in the next Monthly Invoice and GPC must
         remit payment thereof in accordance with Part 6 (Billing and Payment). Conversely, if GPC is required by
         Legal Requirements to remit or pay Taxes that are Generator’s responsibility in this PPA, GPC may deduct
         the amount of any such Taxes from the sums otherwise due to Generator under this PPA. Any refunds
         associated with such Taxes will be handled in the same manner. Nothing in this PPA will obligate or cause
         a Party to pay or be liable to pay any Taxes from which it is exempt under applicable Legal Requirements.


            SALE AND DELIVERY OF CAPACITY AND ENERGY
5.1      Agreement to Sell and Purchase.
         5.1.1. Sale and Purchase of Energy at Point of Interconnection. At all times following the Delivery
         Commencement Date, but subject to the terms of this PPA, Generator must deliver to the POI and sell to
         GPC, free and clear of any liens, taxes, claims, security interests, and other encumbrances, and GPC
         must purchase and receive from Generator at the POI, 100% of the energy produced by the Facility that
         corresponds to the Contracted Capacity, net of Station Service, and all associated Ancillary Services,
         except that: (i) if Generator delivers Excess Energy, GPC will purchase Excess Energy at the Excess
         Energy Price as set forth in Exhibit B (Energy Payment Calculation), and (ii) Generator is prohibited from
         delivering, and GPC is not obligated to purchase or receive, energy (or any associated Ancillary Services)
         in an amount that exceeds the maximum output amount contemplated in the Interconnection Agreement
         (“Interconnection Limit”). For the avoidance of doubt, this PPA does not apply to the sale and purchase
         of energy and Ancillary Services produced by the Facility that corresponds to the Excluded Capacity. The
         delivery of energy to the POI includes the transfer to GPC of all Ancillary Services associated with such

         energy. The Monthly Energy Payments are the exclusive compensation owed to Generator for capacity,
         energy, and Ancillary Services under this PPA.
         5.1.2.   Station Service. Generator is responsible for all Station Service at Generator’s expense.
         5.1.3. Further Provisions. Generator must deliver capacity and energy from the Facility to GPC at the
         POI. The risk of loss of energy will pass from Generator to GPC at the POI. The Facility must be

         transferred hereunder to GPC.

the avoidance of doubt, the Monthly Energy Payment includes all compensation owed to Generator for Ancillary
Services associated with Delivered Energy.


            BILLING AND PAYMENT
6.1      Energy Billing and Payment.
         6.1.1. Monthly Invoice. Subject to the provisions of Section 6.2 (Billing Disputes and Final Accounting),
         by the 10th Day of each Month (commencing with the Month immediately following the Delivery
         Commencement Date), Generator must send the Monthly Invoice to GPC. Payments owed by Generator
         to GPC will be netted against payments due to Generator by GPC.
         6.1.2. Payment. All Monthly Invoices will be due and payable by GPC by the 10th Day after GPC’s
         receipt of the invoice. If the 10th Day is not a Business Day, payment will be due on the next succeeding
         Business Day. Subject to the provisions of Section 6.2 (Billing Disputes and Final Accounting), GPC will
         make payment to Generator under the invoices by the date due in immediately available funds, through
         wire transfer of funds to an account designated by Generator, or other means acceptable to Generator.
         Interest on unpaid amounts will accrue from the date the payments were due at a rate equal to the Interest
         Rate. Each Monthly Invoice will contain a statement explaining in reasonable detail how the invoice was
         calculated under Section 5.2 (Calculation of Monthly Energy Payments).
         6.1.3. Future Qualifying Federal Support Amount Payments. On the Monthly Invoice submitted
         within 30 days of Generator or an Affiliate receiving any Future Qualifying Federal Support Amount,
         Generator shall include the amount received on its Monthly Invoice and shall deduct the Future Qualifying
         Federal Support Amount from the amount owed by GPC to Generator, in accordance with section 6.1.1
         and Exhibit B (Energy Payment Calculation).


6.2      Billing Disputes and Final Accounting.
         6.2.1. Disputed Amounts Withheld. If GPC questions or contests the amount or propriety of any
         payment claimed by Generator to be due under this PPA, GPC must make payment to Generator of
         amounts not in dispute but may withhold amounts disputed in good faith until after the settlement of the
         question or contest under this Section 6.2 (Billing Disputes and Final Accounting).
         6.2.2. Initial Dispute Process. If GPC questions or contests the correctness of any charge or credit,
         GPC will provide Generator with written notice of the amount and the basis for GPC’s question or contest.
         Generator will promptly review the questioned charge or credit and will notify GPC of any error in
         Generator’s determination of amounts owed by GPC and issue an amended invoice in the amount of any
         payment that GPC is required to make in respect of the re-determination. If GPC disputes in good faith
         Generator’s amended invoice amount, the matter must be resolved under the provisions of Part 20
         (Dispute Resolution) applicable to billing disputes. To the extent that Generator disagrees with GPC’s
         basis for questioning the original invoice, Generator will provide a written explanation of its position.

         6.2.3. Correction Timing. Generator will have until the end of one year after the date of delivery of
         energy or Ancillary Services under this PPA to correct any invoice for payment due for the energy and
         associated capacity and deliver a corrected invoice to GPC. GPC will have until the end of one year after
         its receipt of any invoice to question or contest the correctness of any charge or credit made to GPC on
         the invoice. If within such one-year period, GPC has made payment under an invoice and afterwards
         questions or contests the correctness thereof, Generator will not be required to refund any payment
         received from GPC until it is finally determined that Generator’s invoice was in error.
6.3       Interest. If either Party does not make a payment required by this PPA when due, interest at the Interest
Rate will accrue on the overdue payment from the date the payment was due until the overdue payment, together
with interest accrued, is paid in full. If either Party makes a payment under an invoice that is later determined to
have been incorrect, interest at the Interest Rate from the date the overpayment was made will be added to the
overpayment until the overpayment, together with interest, is refunded to the Party. Remittance received by mail,
if mail is a means of payment acceptable to a Party owed the payment, will be accepted without interest charges
if the payment is postmarked on or before the due date. If the due date of any payment falls on a Day other than
a Business Day, the next succeeding Business Day will be the last Day on which payment can be postmarked
without interest charges being assessed. Notwithstanding this Section 6.3 (Interest), no interest will be paid
regarding any Monthly Availability Adjustment except to the extent that such Monthly Availability Adjustment is not
correctly calculated or invoiced under this PPA.
6.4     Billing and Payment Records. Each Party will, until the end of one year after its receipt of any invoice,
make available to the other Party, and each Party may audit the books and records of the other Party as are
necessary for the auditing Party to verify the calculation of the Monthly Energy Payments, and any other invoice,
charge, or payment demand made in connection with this PPA.

Generator) or any other unpaid amounts owed by Generator under this PPA, including to recover delay liquidated
damages under Section 8.3 (Failure to Achieve Commercial Operation by the Required Commercial Operation
Date), damages arising from an Event of Default by Generator, and termination damages arising from termination
of this PPA by GPC for an Event of Default by Generator. In the event of a draw on the Generator Performance
Security, except in the circumstance when GPC establishes an Early Termination Date under Section 17.3.1 (Non-
Defaulting Party Remedies) or this PPA otherwise terminates, Generator must within three Business Days after
the draw on the Generator Performance Security replenish the Generator Performance Security to the full amount
required by Section 7.1 (Generator Performance Security).

demonstrate that Generator and any Generator Guarantor, Generator Guaranty, Letter of Credit or Security
Account is in full compliance with this PPA.

            PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION AND CONSTRUCTION
8.1      Design and Construction of the Project; Commercial Operation of the Facility by RCOD.
         8.1.1. Commercial Operation. The Project will be completed under Prudent Industry Practices and all
         applicable Legal Requirements. The Project (and the Facility) will not achieve “Commercial Operation”
         under this PPA until Generator has satisfied the following criteria: (i) Generator has completed the Project
         to add the Nominal Capability to such electric generating plant; (ii) Generator has demonstrated that the
         Facility is capable of producing energy corresponding to the added Nominal Capability and delivering
         same to the Transmission System through the POI; (iii) the Facility is in compliance with the
         Interconnection Agreement, and the Facility will have demonstrated the reliability of its communication
         systems with the Scheduling Center; (iv) the Facility has successfully completed the Performance Test
         under Section 10.1 (Excluded Capacity; Tested Reliable Capability and Designated Capacity of the
         Facility) or GPC will have determined to its reasonable satisfaction through any combination of testing
         and examination of Facility data that the Facility is fully capable of successfully completing a Performance
         Test; (v) Generator will have provided GPC a certificate reasonably acceptable to GPC, stating that the
         Project has been designed, engineered, constructed, and tested under Prudent Industry Practices and
         that the Facility is capable of performing under the terms of this PPA; and (vi) Generator will have delivered
         to GPC a certificate from a responsible officer of Generator certifying that Generator has obtained all
         Governmental Approvals required under Legal Requirements for the construction of the Project and the
         addition of the Nominal Capability to the electric generating plant through the Project and otherwise for
         the ownership, operation, and maintenance of the Facility under this PPA. Generator must achieve
         Commercial Operation of the Facility under this Section 8.1 (Design and Construction of the Project;
         Commercial Operation of the Facility by RCOD) on or before the RCOD.
         8.1.2. Milestone Schedule. By 250 Days after the date of the Commission Certificate, Generator must
         provide GPC with a Milestone Schedule. Generator must notify GPC of any significant changes in the
         Milestone Schedule and the status of construction as said changes occur (including the reason(s) for the
         change). At GPC’s request, Generator must provide to GPC periodic progress reports in a form
         satisfactory to GPC indicating percentage completion of each major milestone and reporting on significant
         developments that may delay the construction schedule. Promptly after becoming aware of events or
         circumstances that could reasonably be expected to cause a delay in achieving the Commercial Operation
         Date by the RCOD, Generator must provide to GPC for its review and reasonable approval a recovery
         plan setting forth in reasonable detail and with supporting documentation (i) the causes of the event or
         circumstance and the expected delay and (ii) Generator’s plan to recover the lost time and achieve
         Commercial Operation by the RCOD, and, if not by the RCOD, within nine Months after the RCOD. Should
         Generator fail to submit a recovery plan that meets with GPC’s reasonable approval or fail to diligently
         implement the recovery plan, GPC may declare a Generator Event of Default under Section 17.1.5
         (Material Breach of Agreement). Nothing in this Section 8.1.2 (Milestone Schedule) will be construed to
         relieve Generator of any of its obligations set forth under this PPA.
         8.1.3. Inspection Rights. GPC will have the right to reasonably request information regarding the
         status of the Project and to inspect its construction, startup, and testing. Generator must provide the
         information (or cause the information to be provided) to GPC as may be reasonably requested by GPC.
         In addition, Generator must coordinate physical inspections of the Facility (which includes the Project) as
         may be reasonably requested by GPC during and after completion of construction. GPC must provide
         reasonable prior notice to Generator regarding the inspections. All activities of GPC, its designated
         employees, and agents at the Site will be subject to the rules and procedures of Generator (including
         those related to health and safety).
8.2     Permitting. An Event of Default by Generator will arise under Section 17.1.11 (Failure to Obtain Air
Permit) if Generator fails to obtain the Air Permit by the Air Permit Threshold Date or if Generator reasonably

the Transmission Provider by the Effective Date, (ii) enter into an Interconnection Study Agreement with the
Transmission Provider by 30 Days after the Effective Date, (iii) after certification of this PPA by the Commission,
enter into an Interconnection Agreement with the Transmission Provider within 30 Days after the Transmission

                                                                                               PUBLIC DISCLOSURE

Provider presents the Interconnection Agreement to Generator for execution, and (iv) timely comply with all
obligations under the Interconnection Study Agreement and Interconnection Agreement, including timely
submission of required data and documentation and timely payment, as applicable. The Interconnection Study
Agreement must address the full seasonal capability of the Facility. The Interconnection Agreement will be
maintained throughout the Term of this PPA. Generator must promptly provide a copy of, and any amendments
to, the Interconnection Agreement to GPC under the notice provisions of Section 21.4 (Notices). GPC will not be

design, construction, installation, and maintenance of the Interconnection Facilities. Generator is responsible for
determining all transmission-related rules, practices, and policies with which it must comply.
9.2      Meters.
         9.2.1. Metering System Criteria. The Parties will ensure the Metering System is designed, located,
         constructed, installed, owned, operated, and maintained under the Interconnection Agreement and
         Prudent Industry Practices to measure and record the amount of energy delivered from the Facility to the
         POI, to calculate the Facility capacity, and to measure the availability of the Facility. The meters must be
         of a mutually acceptable accuracy range and type. Generator will be responsible for the cost of the
         Metering System that will be installed, owned, operated, and maintained by GPC for the purpose of
         determining the amount of energy delivered to the POI. All Metering System equipment installed by GPC
         will be and remain the personal property of GPC. None of Generator, Generator’s Affiliates, or the
         employees, subcontractors, or contractors of any of them, will make adjustments to the Metering System
         without the written consent of GPC. Generator may, at its own cost, install additional meters or other such
         facilities, equipment, or devices on Generator’s side of the POI as Generator deems necessary or
         appropriate to monitor the measurements of the Metering System, except that in all cases GPC will be
         entitled to base its invoiced amounts solely by reference to its own Metering System. Generator will
         reasonably establish the telemetering equipment that is necessary to coordinate the Facility with the
         Scheduling Center, and Generator must, at its sole cost, install or cause the installation of such
         telemetering equipment. The telemetered data will be delivered by Generator to the electrical switchyard
         of the Facility.
         9.2.2. Inspection. GPC will inspect and test the Metering System at the times as will conform to Prudent
         Industry Practices, but not less often than once biennially. Generator will be responsible for all costs and
         expenses incurred in connection with such inspections or tests.
         9.2.3. Adjustments. If the Metering System fails to register, or if the measurement made by a metering
         device is found upon testing to vary by more than 0.5% from the measurement made by the standard
         meter used in the test, an adjustment will be made correcting all measurements of energy made by the
         Metering System during: (i) the actual period when inaccurate measurements were made by the Metering
         System, if that period can be determined to the mutual satisfaction of the Parties; or (ii) if the actual period
         cannot be determined to the mutual satisfaction of the Parties, the second half of the period from the date
         of the last test of the Metering System to the date the failure is discovered or the test is made
         (“Adjustment Period”). If the Parties are unable to agree on the amount of the adjustment to be applied
         to the Adjustment Period, the amount of the adjustment will be determined: (a) by correcting the error if
         the percentage of error is ascertainable by calibration, tests, or mathematical calculation; or (b) if not so
         ascertainable, by estimating on the basis of deliveries made under similar conditions during the period
         since the last test. Within 30 Days after the determination of the amount of any adjustment, GPC must
         pay Generator any additional amounts then due for deliveries of energy during the Adjustment Period or
         GPC will be entitled to a credit against any subsequent payments for energy, as the case may be.
         9.2.4. Inspection Rights. GPC and its representatives will be entitled to be present at any test,
         inspection, maintenance, adjustment, and replacement of any part of the Metering System relating to
         obligations under this PPA.
9.3      Commercial Operation Delay Caused by Transmission System Capability.
         9.3.1. RCOD Extension. If Generator’s startup and testing activities for the Facility are delayed, as a
         critical-path item on the Milestone Schedule, solely and directly by (i) if GPC is the Transmission Provider,
         a delay in the construction of Interconnection Facilities under the schedule under the Interconnection
         Agreement for which the Transmission Provider is responsible under the Interconnection Agreement, or
         (ii) a delay by GPC in timely ensuring that the Transmission System is capable of providing or receiving
         energy to reasonably accommodate Generator’s startup and testing activities for the Project under the

or analysis prepared by GPC in determining such loss factor.


            TESTED RELIABLE CAPACITY; DESIGNATED CAPACITY
10.1     Excluded Capacity; Tested Reliable Capacity and Designated Capacity of the Facility.
         10.1.1 Performance Testing – Excluded Capacity. Generator will determine the Tested Reliable
         Capacity of the biomass electric generating plant at the Site prior to the modification of the Facility by the
         Project by conducting a Performance Test pursuant to Exhibit D (Performance Testing Procedures) within
         the six-month period prior to the modification of the generating plant by the Project (such Tested Reliable
         Capacity prior to the Project, the “Excluded Capacity”). The determination of the Excluded Capacity will
         be subject to GPC’s written approval, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld. Such determination
         of the Excluded Capacity will be inserted and acknowledged by the Parties in Attachment 1 to Exhibit
         B (Excluded Capacity).
         10.1.2 Project Performance Testing Standards and Reports. The Tested Reliable Capacity and
         Designated Capacity of the Facility after modification of the Facility by the Project must be established
         under Exhibit A (Capacity; Availability). Performance Tests must be conducted under Exhibit D
         (Performance Testing Procedures). Upon completion by Generator of any Performance Test, Generator
         must promptly provide to GPC a complete written report, under Exhibit D (Performance Testing
         Procedures), of the Performance Test, certified by a responsible officer of Generator, for GPC’s review
         and verification. Following the Delivery Commencement Date, Generator must cooperate with GPC’s
         request for information concerning the performance of the Facility that GPC may reasonably request.
10.2      Disputes Concerning Performance Tests. If the Parties disagree regarding the Performance Test
results, the dispute will be resolved under the provisions of Part 20 (Dispute Resolution) applicable to Performance
Test results. If the dispute is not resolved by the first Day of any Annual Period, the Tested Reliable Capacity and
Designated Capacity in effect for the Annual Period may not exceed the Tested Reliable Capacity and Designated
Capacity established under Exhibit A (Capacity; Availability) by the most recent undisputed Performance Test,
subject to the outcome of this dispute resolution process.

            OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE
11.1     Operation and Maintenance.
         11.1.1. Generator Conduct Standards. Generator must manage, control, operate, and maintain all parts
         of the Facility in a manner consistent with Prudent Industry Practices and under applicable planning
         standards and operating policies of the SERC and NERC and under the Operating Procedures to be
         developed by the Operating Committee pursuant to Section 11.1.2 (Development of Operating
         Procedures).
         11.1.2. Development of Operating Procedures. Generator and GPC will mutually develop and agree
         upon written Operating Procedures by 12 Months before the Delivery Commencement Date (“Operating
         Procedures”). Topics covered will include: (i) deliveries of energy during startup and testing of the Facility;
         (ii) the method of Day-to-Day communications; (iii) clearance and switching practices; (iv) daily capacity
         availability and energy reports; (v) Facility operations log; (vi) identification of energy corresponding to
         Contracted Capacity, Excluded Capacity, and Excess Energy; (vii) reactive power output; (viii) technical
         limits regarding Facility operation; (ix) ramp rates for the delivery of power to the Transmission System;
         (x) coordination of maintenance scheduling; (xi) designation of confidential information; (xii) inclusion in
         the Generator’s operating reports to GPC of the amounts, times and circumstances justifying each use of
         natural gas by the Facility, if any, as allowed under Section 12.1 (Fuel Supply) of this PPA; and (xiii) such
         other matters as the Operating Representatives will agree are appropriate. The Operating
         Representatives will be responsible for modifying these Operating Procedures in writing to reflect agreed
         upon changes over the course of the Term. In the event of inconsistency or conflict between the Operating
         Procedures and specific terms of this PPA, the specific terms of this PPA will take precedence.
         The Operating Procedures will be designed to include that during any measurement periods for the
         generation and delivery of energy by the Facility to the POI during the Term, energy subject to a Pre-
         existing Contract will be deemed to be generated and delivered to the POI first, before any energy
         associated with the Contracted Capacity is generated and delivered to the POI pursuant to this PPA.
         Generator will provide GPC with prompt notice of the termination or expiration of the Pre-existing Contract
         and the entry, termination, or expiration of any new contract for the purchase of energy associated with
         the Excluded Capacity. After the termination or expiration of the Pre-existing Contract, Generator may
         provide notice to GPC that, during any forthcoming measurement periods for the generation and delivery
         of energy by the Facility, energy associated with the Excluded Capacity will be deemed to be generated
         and delivered to the POI either before or after energy associated with the Contracted Capacity is
         generated and delivered to the POI pursuant to this PPA. Upon any such election, the Parties will work
         together to mutually develop and agree upon revisions to the Operating Procedures that effect the election
         in a commercially reasonable manner. At GPC’s request and to GPC’s reasonable satisfaction, Generator
         will provide a written acknowledgement from any other offtaker of the Facility confirming Generator’s
         continued compliance with the Generator-offtaker agreement.
         For the avoidance of doubt, if GPC or any other Person is the offtaker under another contract with
         Generator or its Affiliate for energy associated with the Excluded Capacity, the Parties acknowledge that:
         (i) energy delivered to GPC or the other Person under the other contract cannot also be delivered to GPC
         as Excess Energy under this PPA; (ii) energy delivered under this PPA as Excess Energy cannot also be
         delivered to GPC or the other Person under the other contract; and (iii) the Parties will establish
         reasonable operating procedures to clearly distinguish energy being delivered to GPC under this PPA and
         energy being delivered to GPC or other Person from the Facility under the other contract to ensure, among
         other things, that GPC is not paying under this PPA and neither GPC nor the other Person is paying under
         the other contract for the delivery of the same energy and Ancillary Services.
         11.1.3. Safety Procedures. Generator must employ at the Facility all safety devices and safety practices
         required by Prudent Industry Practices. Generator must keep accurate records of any accident or other
         occurrence at the Site that results in injury to Persons or damage to property. Generator must provide to
         GPC reasonable access to these records upon not less than seven Days’ notice during normal business
         hours but will not be required to provide access to employment records regarding Facility personnel.
         11.1.4. Qualified Personnel. During the Term, Generator must employ qualified and trained personnel
         for management, operation, and maintenance of the Facility.

11.2     Maintenance Scheduling.
         11.2.1. Maintenance Schedules. Commencing two Months before the Delivery Commencement Date
         and by September 1 of each year afterwards or such other date as may be set forth in the Operating
         Procedures, Generator must submit to GPC maintenance schedules, including the scope of the
         maintenance, and outage plans for the Facility that conform to Prudent Industry Practices for similar
         equipment, including in terms of frequency and duration (“Maintenance Schedules”), for the next four
         Annual Periods or the number of such Annual Periods remaining in the Term, whichever is less. Generator
         will be entitled to schedule at least one Maintenance Outage of up to twenty-one (21) Days and a second
         Maintenance Outage of up to seven (7) Days during each Annual Period, which outages will be
         approximately four (4) months apart. Generator must not schedule any maintenance of the Facility during
         any of the Months of May, June, July, August, or September of any Annual Period, except as provided
         below with regard to Extended Outages, that would decrease the capacity output of the Facility below the
         Designated Capacity1 without the prior written consent of GPC. GPC will have 30 Days to review the
         proposed Maintenance Schedules and may approve or reject the Maintenance Schedules in whole or in
         part. The Maintenance Schedules are subject to the approval of GPC, which approval will not be
         unreasonably withheld or delayed; except that any determination by GPC to disapprove a major inspection
         as defined by the maintenance documents of the original equipment manufacturer (“Major Inspection”)
         in May or December, or both, will not be considered unreasonable. Subject to compliance with the terms
         herein, Generator shall have the right, during the term of this PPA, to include one (1) maintenance outage
         not to exceed forty (40) continuous days in a Maintenance Schedule (the “Extended Outage”). The
         Extended Outage may not be scheduled in January, February, May, June, July, August, September, or
         December of any Annual Period. If any portion of the Maintenance Schedules is rejected by GPC,
         Generator must resubmit revised Maintenance Schedules to GPC within 30 Days after GPC’s rejection
         and GPC and Generator agree to use best efforts to promptly develop Maintenance Schedules that are
         mutually acceptable to the Parties considering the burdens that GPC’s changes impose on Generator
         compared to the burdens avoided by GPC as a result of the changes. Any dispute concerning this Section
         11.2.1 will be resolved under the provisions of Part 20 (Dispute Resolution) applicable to Maintenance
         Schedule disputes. The outages scheduled in the final, approved Maintenance Schedule will be the
         “Scheduled Outages” for purposes of this PPA.
         11.2.2. Maintenance Outages. In addition to Scheduled Outages, Generator may request an unlimited
         number of Maintenance Outages during any Annual Period. Generator will request each Maintenance
         Outage at least 24 hours in advance and at least one Business Day in advance. The request must identify
         the equipment and Designated Capacity that will not be available and the proposed start time and duration
         of the Maintenance Outage. GPC must respond to Generator’s request as soon as reasonably practicable.
         Generator must not take a Maintenance Outage without GPC’s prior written or telephonic consent, and
         such consent will not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; except that the Parties
         acknowledge that it will be reasonable for GPC to deny any request for a Maintenance Outage if GPC
         reasonably believes that it will need energy output from the Facility at a level that would require the
         availability of the equipment that is proposed to be Unavailable during the Maintenance Outage. GPC will
         have the right to revoke its consent to a Maintenance Outage if changed conditions require energy output
         from the Designated Capacity scheduled to be Unavailable during the Maintenance Outage. If GPC
         reasonably requests Generator to return all or part of that portion of the Facility that is affected by the
         Maintenance Outage to full availability status, Generator must comply as soon as reasonably practical,
         and with consideration of Generator’s mill operations schedule.
         11.2.3. Emergency Procedures. If Generator has a Scheduled Outage and the Scheduled Outage
         occurs or would occur coincident with a System Emergency, GPC will notify Generator of the System
         Emergency. Due to the System Emergency, GPC may request Generator to reschedule the Scheduled
         Outage or, if the Scheduled Outage has begun, to expedite the completion thereof, and Generator must
         comply with the request as soon as reasonably practical.

Term, all Air Permits, including for the operation of the Facility for a minimum of 8,410 hours per Annual Period
throughout the Term, as described in Exhibit E (Facility Description and Site). Generator must provide a copy of

11.5   Availability of Records. Generator must keep complete and accurate records and all other data
necessary for the purposes of proper administration of this PPA under the following guidelines:
         11.5.1. Record Preservation. All records related to the Facility and Generator’s performance under this
         PPA must be maintained for a minimum of five years after the creation of the record or data and for any
         additional period of time required by Legal Requirements or a Governmental Authority; except that such
         records will be kept for as long as is necessary to complete any audit that began or was announced during
         the five-year period. Notwithstanding anything in this PPA to the contrary, if Generator intends to dispose
         of or destroy any such records or data after the five-year period, Generator must provide GPC with 30
         Days’ prior written notice.
         11.5.2. Operating Log. An accurate and up-to-date operating log must be maintained at the Facility with
         records of: (i) real and reactive power production for each clock hour; (ii) changes in operating status and
         scheduled maintenance; (iii) Scheduled Outages, Maintenance Outages, Forced Outages, and Force
         Majeure Events; (iv) any unusual conditions found during inspections; and (v) any significant events
         related to the operation of the Facility.
         11.5.3. Facility Inspection Right. Upon reasonable advance notice and during normal business hours,
         GPC will have the right to examine the records and data relating to the Facility and this PPA, including all
         historical test records relating to the Facility, at the Facility or at a location mutually agreed to by the
         Parties.
         11.5.4. Financial Inspection Right. At the request of GPC throughout the Term of this PPA, Generator
         must provide to GPC public and non-public financial and business information reasonably necessary for
         GPC to make accounting determinations, including Future Qualifying Federal Support. Without limiting
         the foregoing, upon reasonable notice to Generator, GPC and GPC’s independent auditor will have the
         right to inspect the books and records of Generator as are reasonably necessary for GPC to determine
         whether Generator constitutes a VIE and this PPA represents a VIE, or if this PPA must be treated as a
         Finance Lease. To the extent the inspection requires access to confidential information of Generator, the
         information will constitute Confidential Information subject to the provisions of Section 21.13
         (Confidentiality) of this PPA.
11.6      Disclaimer. Generator understands and agrees that GPC’s receipt and review of any material related to
the Project or any physical inspection of the Facility conducted by GPC under any provision of this PPA is solely
for its own information. By conducting such reviews or inspections, GPC makes no endorsement of the design or
representation or warranty of the safety, durability, or reliability of the Facility, all of which are the sole responsibility
of Generator under the terms of this PPA, and GPC will not be deemed to have accepted any condition of the
Facility that is not in full compliance with the terms of this PPA. Generator will in no way represent to any third
party that, as a result of GPC’s receipt and review of any material or any inspections, GPC is in any way
responsible for the engineering or construction soundness of the Facility.

         Generator and GPC, as the case may be, must provide written notice of the appointments to the other
         Party. The appointments may be changed by the maker of the appointment by similar written notice. The

            FUEL SUPPLY; ALLOWANCES
12.1      Fuel Supply. Generator, at its sole expense, will be responsible for obtaining and managing the Biomass
fuel necessary for the operations of the Facility. Generator must develop and maintain a Biomass fuel supply plan
(including any use of natural gas as allowed herein) required for the operation of the Facility to deliver energy
under this PPA (the “Fuel Supply Plan”). Generator must provide the Fuel Supply Plan to GPC and must provide
GPC all updates to the Fuel Supply Plan. As part of the Fuel Supply Plan, Generator must also provide to GPC
all fuel procurement and transportation contracts to verify adequate fuel delivery to the Facility. The Facility must
be fueled by Biomass, except that GPC will allow for natural gas to be used with limitations in the startup and
shutdown of the Facility in accordance with Prudent Industry Practices so long as its limited and necessary use is
clearly demonstrated by Generator to the satisfaction of GPC in each operating report to GPC. Such use of
natural gas must be strictly limited to the extent operationally necessary and essential for the startup or shutdown
of the Facility.
12.2     Allowances.
         12.2.1. Facility NOx and SO2 Allowances. Generator is responsible, at its expense, for all NOx
         Allowances and SO2 Allowances required for NOx Emissions and SO2 Emissions, respectively, from the
         Facility resulting from energy generated by the Facility under this PPA. If such NOx Emissions or SO2
         Emissions exceed the Facility NOx Allowances or Facility SO 2 Allowances, respectively, Generator, at its
         own expense, will be responsible for obtaining all additional NOx Allowances or SO 2 Allowances, as
         applicable, required for the NOx Emissions or SO2 Emissions in excess of the Facility NOx Allowances
         or Facility SO2 Allowances; and no such expenses may be reimbursed by GPC or in any other way passed
         on to GPC.
         12.2.2. Other Allowances Generator Responsibility. Generator will be solely responsible, at its sole
         cost and expense, for any and all other emission allowances other than NOx Allowances and SO 2
         Allowances that are required in connection with the Facility, including for any emissions or energy
         produced therefrom.


            ENERGY NOTICE AND TRANSMISSION
13.1     Required Notices.
         13.1.1. Annual Notice. By September 1 of each calendar year, Generator must provide GPC with the
         time, duration, and magnitude of any planned outages or reduction in capacity for the next calendar year.
         13.1.2. Daily Notice. By 8:00 A.M. ET of each Day, Generator must provide GPC an estimate of the
         hourly amounts of energy to be delivered to the POI for the next Day. Generator must comply with
         reasonable requirements of GPC regarding Day-to-Day or hour-by-hour communications with GPC
         relative to the performance of this PPA.
         13.1.3. Other Notices. Generator must promptly notify GPC of any Unavailability of the Facility or other
         reduction of Designated Capacity, including any Forced Outages, Forced Derates, and Unavailability
         arising from Force Majeure Events. Each such notice must contain information describing the event or
         condition, the beginning date and time of the event or condition, the expected end date and time of the
         event or condition, the amount of energy that Generator expects will be provided during the event or
         condition, and any other information reasonably requested by GPC.

13.2     Coordination. At the request of GPC, Generator must make reasonable efforts to cause the Facility to
control voltage by producing or absorbing reactive power subject to the Technical Limits so long as such actions
do not cause Generator to violate any provisions of its Interconnection Agreement and except that GPC will
reimburse Generator for any incremental costs incurred by Generator (including waiving any negative Facility
Availability impacts directly attributable to Generator’s compliance with the reactive power instructions), in excess
of those costs Generator would have incurred under the Interconnection Agreement, as a result of Generator’s
compliance with any requests.
13.3     System Emergency.
         13.3.1. Process Upon System Emergency. The Parties recognize that GPC is a FERC jurisdictional
         entity subject to the reliability authority of NERC and that, to ensure continuous and reliable electric
         service, GPC operates its system under the operating criteria and guidelines of NERC. If a System
         Emergency is declared and the Scheduling Center, at its sole discretion, identifies the need to modify the
         output of the Facility, the Scheduling Center will notify Generator’s personnel and, if requested,
         Generator’s personnel must immediately place the energy of the Facility within the exclusive control of
         the Scheduling Center for the duration of the System Emergency. In such an event, GPC will ensure that
         the Scheduling Center does not cause the Facility to be operated in a manner that exceeds the Technical
         Limits or any operations-related limits in the Air Permit without the prior consent of Generator, and,
         notwithstanding Generator’s consent, GPC will be responsible for all costs associated with operation of
         the Facility pursuant to such Scheduling Center control, including any penalties imposed on Generator by
         any Governmental Authority or costs incurred by Generator associated with additional maintenance or
         accelerated maintenance, under Prudent Industry Practices, due to the event. Without limiting the
         generality of the foregoing, the Scheduling Center may require Generator’s personnel to raise or lower
         production of energy generated by the Facility, including potential startup or shutdown situations, to
         maintain safe and reliable load levels and voltages on the Transmission System.
         13.3.2. System Emergency Plans. Generator must cooperate with GPC in establishing System
         Emergency plans, including recovery from a local or widespread electrical blackout, voltage reduction to
         effect load curtailment, and other such plans that may be necessary or appropriate under the
         circumstances.
13.4     Effect of Grid Emergencies. The Parties recognize that, under the Interconnection Agreement,
Generator may be required to reduce generation or take certain actions during a Grid Emergency (as defined in
Generator’s Interconnection Agreement) and may be required to disconnect the Facility from the Transmission
System to allow mitigation of system problems and repair or maintenance on the Interconnection Facilities or the
Transmission System. To the extent that Generator is required under the Interconnection Agreement to take any
such action (other than where Generator’s acts or omissions are the cause for the required actions) that will
adversely affect its ability to deliver energy in this PPA, the hours (or equivalent hours) of Unavailability will be
subtracted from the Monthly Hours for the purposes of the Monthly Availability Percentage calculation under
Exhibit A Section B (Calculation of Monthly Availability Percentage). For the avoidance of doubt, Generator is not
entitled to any payment or other compensation under this PPA for energy not delivered as a result of a Grid
Emergency.
13.5    Effect of Insufficient Capability in the Transmission System. If the Transmission System is unable to
receive the energy from the Facility, the hours (or equivalent hours) of Unavailability will be subtracted from the
Monthly Hours for the purposes of the Monthly Availability Percentage calculation under Exhibit A Section B
(Calculation of Monthly Availability Percentage). For the avoidance of doubt, Generator is not entitled to any
payment or other compensation under this PPA for energy not delivered in such event.

be met through any combination of primary insurance and following form excess or umbrella insurance, so long
as the combined limits meet the requirements of this PPA:
         14.1.1. Commercial General Liability. Commercial general liability insurance in an “occurrence” form
         with bodily injury and property damage combined liability limits of not less than twenty million dollars

30 Days before the effective date of any known material change in a required policy.

operation of the Facility or by Generator’s failure to maintain the Facility in satisfactory and safe operating
condition. Generator’s insurance must be primary for any activity arising out of this PPA. Insurance or self-
insurance maintained by GPC or other additional insureds is in excess of Generator’s insurance, contingent and
non-contributory. To the extent allowed by applicable law, GPC and its Representatives must be additional
insureds under the commercial general liability policy, auto liability policy, pollution liability policy and, if applicable,
excess/umbrella policy. To the extent allowed by applicable law, Generator waives, and must require its insurers
to waive, a right of subrogation against GPC and its Representatives for the commercial general liability policy,
auto liability policy, pollution liability policy, umbrella policy, if applicable, and the workers’ compensation policy.
14.4     Proof of Insurance. Before the Effective Date and annually afterwards on the anniversary of the Effective

policy(ies) issued by insurance company(ies) holding a Best rating of at least A- VII and authorized to do business
in the state where the Facility is located. Receipt or acceptance by GPC, with or without objection, of a certificate
of insurance that does not comply with this Part 14 does not operate as a waiver by GPC of Generator’s obligations
under the requirements of this Part 14.
14.5    Payment of Premiums. Generator must pay all premiums and other charges due on each insurance
policy and will keep all coverage in force throughout the Term of this PPA.

PPA, whether or not it is covered by insurance. It is the intent of the Parties, however, that, to the extent there is
