            INDEMNIFICATION
15.1    Scope of Indemnity. Generator expressly agrees to indemnify, hold harmless, and defend GPC and its
Representatives (each an “Indemnified Party”) against all claims, liabilities, fines, costs, or expenses (on an
After-Tax Basis) imposed by Governmental Authorities or arising from loss, damage, or injury to the person or
property of third parties in any manner directly or indirectly related to: (i) the development, construction, use,
ownership, or operation of the Facility; (ii) acts or omissions of Generator or its Representatives in connection with
the performance of, or failure to perform, Generator’s obligations or representations, warranties, or covenants
under this PPA (including any failure to comply with any Consent or Legal Requirement) or any agreement with
another offtaker of the Facility; (iii) a representation or warranty of Generator (or its Affiliate) being false or
misleading in any material respect when made or when deemed made; (iv) activities (including prior uses of third
parties) on Generator’s side of the POI; or (v) any negligence or willful misconduct of Generator or its
Representatives, except to the extent the loss, damage, or injury is the result of the negligence or willful
misconduct of GPC.
15.2     Notice of Proceedings. An Indemnified Party seeking indemnification under this PPA must promptly
notify Generator of any claim or proceeding in respect of which it is to be indemnified. The notice must be given
as soon as reasonably practicable after the Indemnified Party becomes aware of the claim or proceeding. Failure
to give the notice will not excuse an indemnification obligation except to the extent failure to provide notice
prejudices Generator. Generator will assume the defense thereof with counsel designated by Generator; if the
defendants in any such action include both the Indemnified Party and Generator and the Indemnified Party
reasonably concludes that there may be legal defenses available to it that are different from or additional to, or
inconsistent with, those available to Generator, the Indemnified Party will have the right to select and be
represented by separate counsel, at the expense of Generator. If Generator fails to assume the defense of a
claim, the indemnification of which is required under this PPA, the Indemnified Party may, at the expense of
Generator, contest, settle, or pay such claim, except that settlement or full payment of any claim may be made
only with Generator’s consent or, absent such consent, written opinion of the Indemnified Party’s counsel that the
claim is meritorious or warrants settlement.


            FORCE MAJEURE
16.1     No Breach or Liability; Suspension of Performance. If a Force Majeure Event occurs, subject to
compliance with Section 16.2 (Notice of Force Majeure Event) and Section 16.3 (Mitigation), the affected Party
will be excused from performance of its obligations under this PPA, other than payment obligations that accrued
before the declaration of the Force Majeure Event, and will not be construed to be in default in respect of the
obligations to the extent that, and for so long as, failure to perform is due to a Force Majeure Event. However, the
suspension of performance due to a Force Majeure Event will be of no greater scope and of no longer duration
than is required by the Force Majeure Event. Notwithstanding anything in this PPA to the contrary, no Force
Majeure Event will extend this PPA beyond its stated Term.
         16.1.1. RCOD Extension Upon Force Majeure Event. If a Force Majeure Event directly and
         substantially impacts a critical-path item on the Milestone Schedule and as a result prevents Generator
         from achieving Commercial Operation by the RCOD, then the RCOD will be extended by the number of
         Days of the delay caused by the impact to the critical-path item on the Milestone Schedule, except that,
         as a condition to any extension of the RCOD, Generator must comply with Section 16.2 (Notice of Force
         Majeure Event) and Section 16.3 (Mitigation), including Generator undertaking all commercially
         reasonable efforts to avoid, overcome, or otherwise mitigate the delay by revising, rearranging, expediting,
         and accelerating the Milestone Schedule.
16.2      Notice of Force Majeure Event. Following the occurrence of a Force Majeure Event, and as a condition
to relief under Section 16.1 (No Breach or Liability; Suspension of Performance), the affected Party must give the
other Party notice thereof, followed promptly by written notice (and all relevant documentation) if the first notice is
not written, as promptly as possible after the Party becomes aware of the Force Majeure Event, demonstrating
the existence and describing the particulars of the Force Majeure Event, including an analysis of the number of
Days the Force Majeure Event has or will delay the performance of its obligations or satisfaction of any conditions

PPA (Biomass Addition)                                Page 33 of 74

FINAL APPROVED                                                                                2023 BIOMASS RFP
[DATE]                                                                                   BIOMASS ADDITION PPA
                                                                                            PUBLIC DISCLOSURE

under this PPA (including, if Generator is the affected Party, Generator must provide GPC with information
reasonably required to determine the amount of the reduction of the generating capability of the Facility), and
discussing and demonstrating any actions taken and being taken to avoid or minimize the effect of, and rectify,
the Force Majeure Event. The affected Party will have a continuing obligation to deliver to the other Party regular
updated reports and any additional documentation and analysis supporting its claim regarding a Force Majeure
Event. The burden of proof as to whether a Force Majeure Event has occurred and as to the impact of a Force
Majeure Event will be upon the affected Party.
16.3     Mitigation. The affected Party must comply with the following requirements as a condition to the affected
Party’s right to relief under Section 16.1 (No Breach or Liability; Suspension of Performance) due to a Force
Majeure Event: (i) the affected Party must continue to perform its obligations under this PPA to the extent not
affected by the Force Majeure Event; (ii) the affected Party must remedy its inability to perform as soon as
reasonably practicable, except that this Section 16.3 (Mitigation) will not require the settlement of any non-site
specific strike, walkout, lockout or other general labor dispute on terms that, in the sole judgment of the affected
Party, are contrary to its interest; and (iii) when the affected Party can resume performance of its obligations under
this PPA, the affected Party must promptly provide written notice to the other Party, promptly resume the
performance, and provide the other Party with a written certification from an independent, registered engineer
reasonably acceptable to the other Party that the Force Majeure Event has been cured.
16.4     Extended Force Majeure Events.
         16.4.1. Force Majeure Remedy Plan. If the affected Party has reason to believe that a suspension of
         performance due to a Force Majeure Event will continue for a period of six Months or longer following the
         initial suspension of performance resulting from the Force Majeure Event (an “Extended Force Majeure
         Event”), the affected Party must notify the other Party promptly and must submit a “Force Majeure
         Remedy Plan” to the other Party within 30 Days afterwards. In addition, if the other Party has reason to
         believe that a Force Majeure Event will be an Extended Force Majeure Event, the other Party may request
         that the affected Party submit a “Force Majeure Remedy Plan,” which the affected Party must submit to
         the requesting Party within 30 Days after the request. A Force Majeure Remedy Plan will set forth a plan
         and schedule for remedial measures (including necessary repairs, improvements, and changes to
         operations, as applicable) to cure the effects of the Force Majeure Event to enable the affected Party to
         resume full performance of the suspended obligations under this PPA as soon as reasonably practicable.
         16.4.2. Monthly Status Reports During Force Majeure Remedy Plan. While a Force Majeure Remedy
         Plan is in effect, the affected Party must provide Monthly status reports to the other Party regarding the
         implementation of the Force Majeure Remedy Plan, any other measures to remedy the Force Majeure
         Event, any changes to the Force Majeure Remedy Plan, and the expected remaining duration of the
         suspended performance, and must provide any additional relevant information as may be reasonably
         requested by the other Party. The affected Party must modify the Force Majeure Remedy Plan if and as
         needed to achieve the objective of resuming full performance of the suspended obligations under this
         PPA as soon as reasonably practicable.
         16.4.3. Termination Due To Force Majeure Event. The Party not prevented from performing its
         obligations due to the Force Majeure Event may terminate this PPA effective upon 10 Days’ prior written
         notice to the affected Party if: (i) the affected Party fails to provide a Force Majeure Remedy Plan as
         required by this Section 16.4 (Extended Force Majeure Events); or (ii) the affected Party fails to carry out
         the Force Majeure Remedy Plan in a method reasonably designed to achieve the objective of resuming
         full performance of the suspended obligations under this PPA as soon as reasonably practicable; or (iii) the
         affected Party remains unable to perform the suspended obligations under this PPA 12 Months following
         the initial suspension of performance resulting from the Force Majeure Event. For the purposes of
         subsection (iii) of this Section 16.4.3 (Termination Due to Force Majeure Event), the 12-Month period need
         not be continuous if each period of suspension of performance comprising the 12-Month period is the
         result of a common cause such that, if the cause had been cured following the first suspension of
         performance, the additional suspensions of performance would not have occurred.
         16.4.4. No Further Liability or Obligation Following Termination. Upon any termination of this PPA
         as provided in Section 16.4.3 (Termination Due To Force Majeure Event), the Parties will have no further
         liability or obligation to each other except for any obligation arising before the date of the termination.

            DEFAULT AND REMEDIES
17.1   Default by Generator. The occurrence of any of the following events will constitute an Event of Default
by Generator:
         17.1.1. Representation or Warranty Breach. Any representation or warranty made by Generator in this
         PPA or in any certificate or other document delivered to GPC pursuant hereto proves to be incorrect in
         any material respect when made, unless Generator promptly commences and diligently pursues action to
         cause the representation or warranty to become true in all material respects and does so within 30 Days
         after notice thereof has been given to Generator by GPC (unless the cure is not capable of being effected
         within the 30-Day period, in which case Generator will have an additional 30-Day period in which to
         perform the cure) and the cure removes any material adverse effect on GPC of the representation or
         warranty having been incorrect.
         17.1.2. Involuntary Bankruptcy or Insolvency. (A) Generator has a petition filed against it that is not
         stayed, withdrawn, or dismissed within 120 Days after the filing, under any applicable federal or state
         bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, or other similar law or any other case or proceeding to be
         adjudicated a bankrupt or insolvent; or (B) a court having jurisdiction enters: (i) a decree or order for relief
         in respect of Generator in an involuntary case or proceeding under any applicable federal or state
         bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, or other similar law; or (ii) a decree or order, the entry of which
         was sought by an entity other than Generator, adjudicating Generator bankrupt or insolvent, or approving
         as properly filed a petition seeking reorganization, arrangement, adjustment, or composition of or in
         respect of Generator under any applicable federal or state law, or appointing a custodian, receiver,
         liquidator, assignee, trustee, sequestrator, or other similar official of Generator or of any substantial part
         of its affairs.
         17.1.3. Voluntary Bankruptcy or Insolvency. Generator: (i) commences a voluntary case or proceeding
         under any applicable federal or state bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, or other similar law or any
         other case or proceeding to be adjudicated a bankrupt or insolvent; (ii) consents to the entry of a decree
         or order for relief in respect of Generator in any involuntary case or proceeding under any applicable
         federal or state bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, or other similar law or to the commencement of
         any bankruptcy or insolvency case or proceeding against it; (iii) files any petition, answer, or consent
         seeking reorganization or similar relief under any applicable federal or state law that, if granted, would
         have the effect of relieving Generator of any of its obligations; (iv) consents to the filing of any petition or
         to the appointment of or taking possession by a custodian, receiver, liquidator, assignee, trustee,
         sequestrator, or similar official of Generator or of any substantial part of its property; (v) makes an
         assignment for the benefit of creditors; (vi) admits in writing its inability to generally pay its debts as they
         become due; or (vii) takes any action in furtherance of any of the foregoing.
         17.1.4. Guaranty Breach. Generator fails to comply or cause compliance with the Generator
         Performance Security requirements of Section 7.1 (Generator Performance Security), or Generator
         Guarantor breaches any of its obligations under the Generator Guaranty or if any representation or
         warranty made by Generator Guarantor in the Generator Guaranty proves to be incorrect in any material
         respect when made, unless any of the foregoing is cured by the end of the second Business Day following
         receipt of a written notice from GPC of a failure under this Section 17.1.4.
         17.1.5. Material Breach of Agreement. Generator fails to perform or observe any material obligation of
         Generator under this PPA, other than those obligations specifically addressed in Section 17.1 (Default by
         Generator), which failure continues for a period of 30 Days after written notice thereof from GPC unless
         the cure is not capable of being effected within the 30-Day period, in which case Generator will have an
         additional 30-Day period in which to perform the cure.
         17.1.6. Assignment or Change of Control. Generator violates the requirements of Part 19 (Assignment
         and Transfers of Interest) through an assignment or transfer of this PPA or an ownership interest in the
         Facility or through a Change of Control Transaction.
         17.1.7. Failure to Pay GPC. Generator fails to pay GPC any undisputed amount payable by Generator
         to GPC under this PPA for 15 Days after the same has become due and Generator fails to cure the failure
         to pay within 15 Days after receipt of written demand therefor from GPC.
         17.1.8. Unsatisfactory Availability Percentage. The Availability Percentage (as defined below) is below
         60% for any (i) one Summer Season, or (ii) one Winter Season, or (iii) six consecutive Months, except

                  inadequate Tested Reliable Capacity, the Cure Period will be extended for a reasonable additional
                  period of time, which extension will not in any case exceed 420 Days, if Generator satisfies all of
                  the following conditions: by 15 Days before the expiration of the 120-Day Cure Period, Generator
                  must provide to GPC (I) a revised cure plan setting forth a reasonable extension of the Cure
                  Period, not to exceed 420 Days, which revised cure plan and extension will be reasonably
                  acceptable to GPC, and (II) a written certification reasonably acceptable to GPC confirming that
                  in order for Generator to cure the inadequate Tested Reliable Capacity Generator must be
                  afforded the reasonable additional period of time. For the avoidance of doubt, the total duration
                  of the Cure Period, as extended, will not exceed 540 Days.
                  B.    Cure. The cause of the inadequate Tested Reliable Capacity of the Facility will be cured
                  under Section 17.1.9 (Unsatisfactory Tested Reliable Capacity) only if (I) Generator provides GPC
                  with a written certification reasonably acceptable to GPC confirming that the inadequate Tested
                  Reliable Capacity has been cured, and (II) the inadequate Tested Reliable Capacity is increased
                  to a value such that the Tested Reliable Capacity of the Facility, as demonstrated by the most
                  recent Performance Test, minus the Excluded Capacity is equal to or greater than 70% of the
                  Nominal Capability as demonstrated by the most recent Performance Test. Throughout the
                  duration of any Cure Period, the Designated Capacity will be determined pursuant to Exhibit A
                  Section A.3 (Designated Capacity) based on the most recent Performance Test.

17.3     Remedies.
         17.3.1. Non-Defaulting Party Remedies. If an Event of Default occurs during the Term, the non-
         defaulting Party (the “Non-Defaulting Party”) may, for so long as the Event of Default is continuing,
         subject to the provisions of Part 20 (Dispute Resolution), take one or more of the following actions:
         (i) establish a date (which date will be no more than 10 Business Days after the Non-Defaulting Party
         delivers written notice of the date to the defaulting Party (the “Defaulting Party”)) on which this PPA will
         terminate (the “Early Termination Date”), (ii) proceed by appropriate proceedings under this PPA at law,
         in equity, or otherwise, to protect and enforce its right to damages (actual or liquidated) or, where the
         Event of Default is one other than the failure to pay money, equitable relief, including specific performance,
         and (iii) immediately cease performance or withhold any payments, or both, due in respect of this PPA.
         17.3.2. Termination Payment. If an Early Termination Date has been established, and the Non-
         Defaulting Party has not successfully pursued an action for specific performance or is not excused from
         the payment of damages under Section 17.1.14 (Consolidation), the Non-Defaulting Party will in good
         faith calculate its Gains, Losses, and Costs resulting from the termination of this PPA, aggregate the
         Gains, Losses, and Costs into a single net amount, and notify the Defaulting Party. If the Non-Defaulting
         Party’s aggregate Losses and Costs exceed its aggregate Gains, the Defaulting Party will, unless it

         17.3.3. Determination of Losses and Costs. Subject to the provisions of Section 11.3.1 (Calculation
         Upon Generator Event of Default) the Gains, Losses, and Costs will be determined by comparing the cost
         under this PPA of the capacity and energy that would be available under this PPA for the remainder of the
         Term had this PPA not been terminated to the market price of capacity and energy of equivalent reliability
         (including equivalent fuel mix and Ancillary Services) for the remaining Term (had this PPA not been
         terminated). For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in Part 7 (Performance Security) is intended to limit
         liability under this Section 17.3 (Remedies). To ascertain the market price, the Non-Defaulting Party may
         consider, among other evidence, the settlement prices of NYMEX energy futures contracts, quotations
         from leading dealers in energy and gas swap contracts, offers for replacement capacity and energy, or
         bids to purchase the remaining capacity and energy that was to be sold under this PPA, in either case
         made by bona fide third parties (including offers received by the Non-Defaulting Party in response to any
         request for proposals for capacity and energy contracts), all adjusted for the length of the remaining Term
         (had this PPA not been terminated) and differences in locational basis (including costs of transmission
         investments and transmission service), reliability, and any other considerations affecting value. Neither
         Party will be required to enter into replacement transactions to determine the Termination Payment. As
         used in Sections 17.3.2 (Termination Payment) and 17.3.3 (Determination of Losses and Costs): (i)
         “Costs” means brokerage fees, commissions, and other similar transaction costs and expenses
         reasonably incurred by the Party either in terminating any agreement that it has entered into to fulfill its
         obligations in this PPA or entering into new agreements that replace this PPA, and attorneys’ fees, if any,
         incurred in connection with enforcing its rights under this PPA; (ii) “Gains” means an amount equal to the
         economic benefit determined on a mark to market basis (exclusive of Costs), if any, to the Non-Defaulting
         Party resulting from the termination of this PPA; and (iii) “Losses” means an amount equal to the economic
         loss determined on a mark to market basis (exclusive of Costs), if any, to the Non-Defaulting Party
         resulting from the termination of this PPA.
17.4    Rights of Specific Performance. In the case of an Event of Default, the Parties recognize that any
remedy at law may be inadequate because this PPA is unique and because the actual damages of the Non-
Defaulting Party may exceed the amount of any guaranty or other collateral available to the Non-Defaulting Party.
The Non-Defaulting Party will be entitled to pursue an action for specific performance and the Defaulting Party
waives all of its rights to assert as a defense to the action that the Non-Defaulting Party’s remedy at law is
adequate. For the avoidance of doubt, the Non-Defaulting Party will not be entitled to receive both specific
performance and a Termination Payment from the Defaulting Party.
17.5   Limitation of Remedies, Liability and Damages. THE PARTIES CONFIRM THAT THE EXPRESS
REMEDIES AND MEASURES OF DAMAGES PROVIDED IN THIS PPA SATISFY THE ESSENTIAL
PURPOSES OF THIS PPA FOR BREACH OF ANY PROVISION FOR WHICH AN EXPRESS REMEDY OR
MEASURE OF DAMAGES IS PROVIDED, SUCH EXPRESS REMEDY OR MEASURE OF DAMAGES WILL BE
THE SOLE AND EXCLUSIVE REMEDY, THE OBLIGOR’S LIABILITY WILL BE LIMITED AS SET FORTH IN
SUCH PROVISION, AND ALL OTHER REMEDIES OR DAMAGES AT LAW OR IN EQUITY ARE WAIVED. IF
NO REMEDY OR MEASURE OF DAMAGES IS EXPRESSLY PROVIDED IN THIS PPA, THE OBLIGOR’S
LIABILITY WILL BE LIMITED TO DIRECT ACTUAL DAMAGES ONLY, SUCH DIRECT ACTUAL DAMAGES
WILL BE THE SOLE AND EXCLUSIVE REMEDY, AND ALL OTHER REMEDIES OR DAMAGES AT LAW OR
IN EQUITY ARE WAIVED. UNLESS EXPRESSLY PROVIDED IN THIS PPA, AND EXCEPT FOR THE PAYMENT
OF LIQUIDATED DAMAGES SPECIFIED IN THIS PPA, NEITHER PARTY NOR THEIR AFFILIATES WILL BE

            CHANGE OF LAW
18.1     New GHG Law.
         18.1.1. Responsibility for GHG Charges. In the event of the enactment of a New GHG Law by any
         Governmental Authority, Generator will be responsible at its own expense for any GHG Charges arising
         from or attributed to any New GHG Law, and in no event will such GHG Charges be paid for, reimbursed
         by, or in any other way passed on to, GPC. Generator will be required to use all reasonable steps to
         mitigate the cost or amount of such GHG Charges, including GHG Credits, if any, under Section 18.1.2
         (GHG Credits).
         18.1.2. GHG Credits. Generator must use GHG Credits including those allocated to or for the Facility, or
         otherwise granted to or received by Generator for the Facility, to avoid or mitigate GHG Charges under
         Section 18.1.1 (Responsibility for GHG Charges). In addition, if Generator purchases, is allocated, is
         issued, or may obtain GHG Credits for a portion of or its entire fleet of generating units, Generator must,
         at no cost to GPC, reserve a proportional amount of such GHG Credits to mitigate any GHG Charges
         under Section 18.1.1 (Responsibility for GHG Charges). For purposes of this Section 18.1.2 (GHG
         Credits), all references to “Generator” will be deemed to include Generator’s Affiliates or other entity to
         which GHG Credits may be available for use by or for the Facility. The proportional amount of GHG
         Credits will be calculated based on the method, formula, or other similar calculation by which the
         Governmental Authority used to determine the amount of the GHG Credits attributable to each generating
         unit compared to the sum of all GHG Credits for all generating units of Generator. Generator must provide
         GPC with all information reasonably requested by GPC to document GHG Credits available or applicable
         to Generator and Generator’s compliance with this Section 18.1.2 (GHG Credits).
         18.1.3. Restrictions. Generator must not transfer, apply, use, or provide any other Person’s rights
         regarding GHG Credits that Generator is required to use to mitigate GHG Charges under Section 18.1.2
         (GHG Credits). If and to the extent that any GHG Credits for an Annual Period addressed by Section
         18.1.2 (GHG Credits), prorated for the purposes of this Section 18.1.3 (Restrictions) for the respective

18.2     Change of Law.
         18.2.1. Change of Law Notice. If Generator determines that any Change of Law Capital Expenditures
         will be incurred as a result of a Change of Law (including costs less than the Threshold Amount),
         Generator must notify GPC of a Change of Law by six Months after the enactment of the applicable
         Change of Law (“Change of Law Notice”). The Change of Law Notice must include a discussion of the
         relevant Change of Law and its applicability to the Facility and the delivery of energy to the POI under this
         PPA, Generator’s plan to comply with the Change of Law (including the additional or different equipment
         at the Facility or other modification of the Facility required to comply with the Change of Law), and
         reasonable documentation of Generator’s determination of Change of Law Capital Expenditures (or
         estimate of Change of Law Capital Expenditures if actual costs are not known), and Generator must
         provide periodic updates to GPC regarding Generator’s compliance plan and Change of Law Capital
         Expenditures. Generator must provide any additional relevant information as may reasonably requested
         by GPC.
         18.2.2. Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures.
                  A.    If one or more Change of Laws would cause Generator to incur Change of Law Capital
                  Expenditures (in the aggregate), as prorated in accordance with the definition of Change of Law
                  Capital Expenditures, in excess of four dollars per kilowatt ($4.00/kW) multiplied by the Nominal
                  Capability in kW in any given Annual Period (the “Threshold Amount”), and, if Generator
                  submitted a Change of Law Notice(s) for the Change of Law(s) under Section 18.2.1 (Change of
                  Law Notice), Generator may, through written notice to GPC (“Excess Capital Expenditures
                  Notice”), request GPC’s approval, in GPC’s sole discretion, of Generator’s recovery of the
                  incremental amount of capital expenditures in excess of the Threshold Amount (such excess
                  amount, the “Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures”) through an adjustment to the
                  Energy Price, except that no adjustment will be allowed to the Energy Price for any calendar year
                  before Generator actually incurred Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures. For the
                  avoidance of doubt, the prorated amount of Change of Law Capital Expenditures that corresponds
                  to the Excluded Capacity will not accrue to the Threshold Amount and will not be included in any
                  Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures and Generator otherwise may not seek recovery of
                  the prorated amount of Change of Law Capital Expenditures that corresponds to the Excluded
                  Capacity. Generator may not seek recovery of any Change of Law Capital Expenditures for which
                  Generator did not submit a Change of Law Notice under Section 18.2.1 (Change of Law Notice).
                  The Excess Capital Expenditures Notice will supplement the Change of Law Notice, including
                  addressing in detail the Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures and setting forth Generator’s
                  calculations for the proposed increase in the Energy Price, as determined under this Section
                  18.2.2. Generator will be responsible for demonstrating that Generator’s proposed plan for
                  complying with the Change of Law is reasonable and conforms with Prudent Industry Practices
                  and that the Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures are reasonable, consistent with Prudent
                  Industry Practices, required for compliance with the Change of Law, and otherwise in compliance
                  with Section 18.2 (Change of Law). Generator must promptly provide any and all other information
                  reasonably requested by GPC in connection with GPC’s analysis of and response to Generator’s
                  Excess Capital Expenditures Notice.
                  B.     For purposes of calculating any adjustment to the Energy Price associated with capitalized
                  additions or modifications to the Facility (determined in accordance with GAAP), the Parties will,
                  each acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner, establish an appropriate
                  annual fixed charge rate for application to the original capital cost of the additions, modifications,
                  or other capital expenditures. This calculation will represent the total cost associated with the
                  identified addition or modification, including depreciation, carrying costs, and any other cost or
                  expense item related to capital investments.

         18.2.3. GPC Election Notice. By 365 Days after receipt of Generator’s Excess Capital Expenditures
         Notice, GPC must inform Generator by written notice of whether GPC, in GPC’s sole discretion, accepts
         or rejects Generator’s proposed adjustment to the Energy Price to recover Excess Change of Law Capital
         Expenditures (“GPC Election Notice”); if GPC does not notify Generator of GPC’s decision within the
         365-Day period, GPC will be deemed to have rejected Generator’s proposed adjustment to the Energy
         Price. For the avoidance of doubt, under no circumstances will GPC’s rejection of a proposed adjustment
         to the Energy Price and Generator’s recovery of Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures constitute
         an Event of Default under Part 17 (Default and Remedies) of this PPA.
         18.2.4. Generator Response Notice.
                  A.    If GPC, in its sole discretion, rejects Generator’s request, or if GPC is deemed under
                  Section 18.2.3 (GPC Election Notice) to have rejected Generator’s request, to recover Excess
                  Change of Law Capital Expenditures addressed in Generator’s Excess Capital Expenditures
                  Notice, Generator must provide written notice to GPC (the “Generator Response Notice”) by
                  the Generator Response Deadline of whether Generator elects to (i) pay for the Change of Law
                  Capital Expenditures (including Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures), or (ii) terminate
                  this PPA effective as of the date set forth in the Generator Response Notice (which date will be
                  no earlier than 365 Days after the date the Generator Response Notice is provided to GPC). The
                  “Generator Response Deadline” is the date that is 30 Days after the earlier of (a) the date of the
                  GPC Election Notice, or (b) 365 Days after GPC’s receipt of Generator’s Excess Capital
                  Expenditures Notice if GPC did not provide a GPC Election Notice. If Generator does not provide
                  a Generator Response Notice to GPC by the Generator Response Deadline, Generator will be
                  deemed to have waived the option to terminate this PPA as a result of the relevant Change of
                  Law(s) and Change of Law Capital Expenditures and will be deemed to have elected to pay for
                  the Change of Law Capital Expenditures (including Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures).
                  B.     Notwithstanding anything in this PPA to the contrary, if Generator elects to terminate this
                  PPA in a Generator Response Notice provided to GPC by the Generator Response Deadline,
                  GPC will have the right to elect by written notice, delivered to Generator within 60 Days after such
                  Generator Response Notice, to accept Generator’s proposed adjustment to the Energy Price as
                  set forth in Generator’s Excess Capital Expenditures Notice to recover Excess Change of Law
                  Capital Expenditures, and in such case this PPA will not terminate and will continue in full effect
                  with the adjustment to the Energy Price. If GPC does not provide such written notice within the
                  60-Day period, GPC will be deemed to have waived the election and this PPA will terminate in
                  accordance with the Generator Response Notice on the date set forth in the Generator Response
                  Notice (provided the termination date will be no earlier than 365 Days after the date the Generator
                  Response Notice is provided). Generator will be responsible for all Change of Law Capital
                  Expenditures incurred before the effective date of any such termination. Following the effective
                  date of any such termination, neither Party will have any further liability to the other Party except
                  for any obligations incurred before the effective date of the termination.
         18.2.5. No Further Energy Price Adjustment. The Parties acknowledge that, except as provided in
         Sections 18.2.2 (Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures), 18.2.3 (GPC Election Notice), and 18.2.4
         (Generator Response Notice), the Energy Price will not be adjusted as a result of a Change of Law or
         Change of Law Capital Expenditures. If GPC has elected under Section 18.2.3 (GPC Election Notice) or
         Section 18.2.4 (Generator Response Notice) to accept Generator’s proposed adjustment to the Energy
         Price to recover Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures, Generator may not seek any additional
         adjustment to the Energy Price for the Change of Law(s) addressed in the GPC election (including for any
         additional or different Change of Law Capital Expenditures arising from the Change of Law(s)). For the
         avoidance of doubt, any election by GPC under Section 18.2.3 (GPC Election Notice) or Section 18.2.4
         (Generator Response Notice) to allow Generator to recover Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures
         will apply only to the Change of Law and Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures addressed in the
         GPC election.
         18.2.6. Limits to GPC Financial Responsibility. Generator acknowledges and agrees that, except as
         provided in Part 18 (Change of Law): (i) GPC will not be responsible for any costs or expenses incurred
         by Generator in connection with the Facility or the performance of Generator’s obligations under this PPA
         that result from new or different or other changes in Legal Requirements (including any change in an
         interpretation of any Legal Requirement); and (ii) in no event will the payments required to be made by

            ASSIGNMENT AND TRANSFERS OF INTEREST
19.1     Assignment and Assumption of Obligations.
         19.1.1. Generator.
                  A.    Generator may not assign this PPA or any portion thereof to any Person without the prior
                  written consent of GPC. Any proposed assignee of this PPA must (i) agree to assume assignor’s
                  obligations under this PPA, and (ii) deliver to GPC the assurances regarding its creditworthiness
                  and its ability to perform all obligations of Generator under this PPA, as GPC may reasonably
                  request. Any assignment of this PPA made in compliance with the preceding sentences will
                  constitute an acceptance and assumption of the obligations by the assignee.
                  B.     Notwithstanding Section 19.1.1.A (Assignment and Assumption of Obligations: Generator),
                  Generator may, without the consent of GPC, assign this PPA to a lender for collateral security
                  purposes in connection with any financing or the refinancing of the Facility, and, in connection
                  therewith, GPC agrees to execute a reasonable written consent to the collateral assignment in a
                  form acceptable to GPC should the financing party reasonably request such consent, except that
                  the collateral assignment will not place any limitation on GPC’s rights under this PPA or expand
                  the liability, risks, or obligations imposed on GPC under this PPA.
                  C.     Upon reasonable request to GPC, GPC agrees to execute a written confirmation that, if
                  true, to the best of GPC’s knowledge when the request is made, Generator is not in default of this
                  PPA.
         19.1.2. GPC. GPC may not assign this PPA or any portion thereof to any Person other than a
         Creditworthy Affiliate without the prior written consent of Generator and approval by the Commission.
19.2      Other Restrictions. Generator agrees that, without the prior written consent of GPC, there will be no
(i) assignment or transfer of any interest in the Facility, (ii) Change of Control Transaction regarding Generator, or
(iii) delegation by Generator of the operational responsibility for the Facility.
19.3      Reimbursement for GPC’s Costs from Transfers or Assignments. Generator agrees that, if Generator
assigns or transfers an interest in the Facility or this PPA, as such transactions are described in Section 19.1
(Assignment and Assumption of Obligations) and Section 19.2 (Other Restrictions), Generator will pay GPC the
amount of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) per occurrence for each and any proposed transaction and will
pay to GPC the amount of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) per occurrence for each and any request for an estoppel
under Section 19.1.1.C (Assignment and Assumption of Obligations: Generator). For the avoidance of doubt, if
Generator requests GPC’s consent under Section 19.1.1 (Assignment and Assumption of Obligations: Generator)
or Section 19.2 (Other Restrictions), GPC undertakes drafting of consent documents or amendments to provide
the consent, and Generator afterwards fails to consummate the proposed transaction, GPC reserves the right, in
its sole discretion, to require Generator to provide reimbursement to GPC under this Section 19.3 (Reimbursement
for GPC’s Costs from Transfers or Assignments).
19.4      General Requirements. Any consent required by Section 19.1 (Assignment and Assumption of
Obligations) or Section 19.2 (Other Restrictions) will not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, except
that neither Party will be required to accept any limitation of its rights under this PPA or expansion of the liability,
risks, or obligations imposed on it under this PPA (including changes in accounting treatment). It will be reasonable
for either Party to condition its consent required by Part 19 (Assignment and Transfers of Interest) on the execution
of amendments to this PPA that are reasonably determined by such Party to be necessary to preserve the value
and protection afforded to such Party under this PPA. It will be a condition of any assignment, transfer, Change of
Control Transaction, or other disposition regarding this PPA and the Facility under Section 19.1 (Assignment and
Assumption of Obligations) or Section 19.2 (Other Restrictions) that Generator Performance Security required
under Section 7.1 (Generator Performance Security), if applicable, will remain in place notwithstanding the

            DISPUTE RESOLUTION
20.1     Notice of Dispute. Either Party (“Disputing Party”) may give notice to the other Party (“Responding
Party”) that the Responding Party is not performing in accordance with the terms and conditions of this PPA. The
notice of dispute will describe with specificity the basis for the Disputing Party’s belief and may propose a
resolution of the dispute (“Notice of Dispute”).
20.2     Dispute Resolution, Arbitration.
         20.2.1. Except as provided in Section 17.5 (Limitation of Remedies, Liability and Damages), any dispute
         or claims arising under this PPA that cannot be resolved by the Parties through negotiation by the
         Parties' managers within thirty (30) Days after the Notice of Dispute will be referred to senior
         executives (president or a vice president) of the Parties for resolution, which executives shall have
         the authority to decide or resolve the matter in dispute. If such senior executives are unable to resolve
         any such dispute or claim to the mutual satisfaction of the Parties within thirty (30) Days after such
         matter has been referred to such senior executives by the Parties' managers, then any such dispute
         or claim shall be resolved in accordance with Section 20.2.2.
         20.2.2. In the event the Parties are unable to resolve a dispute as provided in Section 20.2.1, (a)
         the Parties agree to arbitrate those disputes described in Section 20.2.3 using the procedures
         provided in such subsection, and (b) in the case of any dispute that is not described in the Section
         20.2.3, either Party may pursue its rights and remedies available under other provisions of this PPA.
         20.2.3. Arbitration. In the event the dispute concerns the calculation of a Termination Payment
         pursuant to Section 17.3.2 (Termination Payment), or a billing dispute under Section 6.2 (Billing
         Disputes and Final Accounting), then the Parties agree to arbitrate such dispute in accordance with
         the following procedures:
                  A. At the request of either Party upon written notice to the other party (a “Demand”), the
                  dispute will be finally settled by binding arbitration before a single arbitrator in accordance
                  with the Expedited Procedures of the Commercial Arbitration Rules (the “Rules”) of the AAA
                  then in effect, except as modified herein. The Demand must include statements of the facts
                  and circumstances surrounding the dispute, the legal obligation breached by the other Party,
                  the amount in controversy and the requested relief accompanied by all relevant documents
                  supporting the Demand.
                  B. The arbitration will be held in Atlanta, Georgia and will be governed by the United States
                  Arbitration Act, 9 U.S.C. §§1 et seq.
                  C. Unless the Parties otherwise agree, the arbitrator selected will have a reasonable
                  degree of expertise in the subject matter of the dispute, will not have provided services to
                  either Party or any of their respective Affiliates within the last five (5) year s and will be
                  selected from a national panel of potential arbitrators.
                  D. The award will be in writing (stating the award and the reasons therefor) and will be
                  final and binding upon the Parties and will be the sole and exclusive remedy between the
                  Parties regarding any claims, counterclaims, issues or accountings presented to t he
                  arbitrator. The arbitrator will be authorized in his or her discretion to grant pre -award and
                  post-award interest at commercial rates. Judgment upon any award may be entered in any
                  court having jurisdiction. Each of the Parties consents to service of process by registered
                  mail at its address set forth herein and agrees that its consent to service of process by mail
                  is made for the express benefit of the other Party.
                  E.   This PPA and the rights and obligations of the Parties will remain in full force and effect
                  pending the award in any arbitration proceedings hereunder.

                  F.    Unless otherwise ordered by the arbitrators, each Party will bear its own costs and fees,
                  including attorneys’ fees and expenses. The Parties expressly agree that the arbitrators will
                  have no power to consider or award any form of damages barred by Section 17.5, or any
                  other multiple or enhanced damages, whether statutory or common law. With respect to

                  20.2.3.


20.3      Injunctive Relief. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Part 20 (Dispute Resolution), the Parties
acknowledge that an award of damages may not afford complete relief or furnish an adequate legal remedy as
between them (such as when Generator’s Event of Default arises from Generator’s actions designed to achieve
an economic gain by selling energy, capacity, or Ancillary Services to a third party in violation of this PPA).
Accordingly, a Party will be permitted to seek, under applicable laws, procedures, and the terms of this PPA,
injunctive relief relating to the performance of this PPA from an arbitrator, a Governmental Authority of appropriate
jurisdiction, or a court of competent jurisdiction located in Atlanta, Fulton County, Georgia. The Parties expressly
agree that this Section 20.3 (Injunctive Relief) does not present a question of substantive arbitrability and waive
any right to have an arbitrator decide whether preliminary injunctive relief is available in court. In the event of entry
of any interlocutory injunctive relief, the Party against whom the relief is entered waives the right to have a bond
or security posted pending resolution of the dispute giving rise to the issuance of the injunction.
20.4     Continued Performance. The Parties will continue performing their respective obligations under this PPA
while the dispute is being resolved, unless and until such obligations are terminated or expire under the provisions
of this PPA.

                                  EXHIBIT A – CAPACITY; AVAILABILITY


A.       Contracted Capacity; Tested Reliable Capacity; Designated Capacity:
         1.     Contracted Capacity Cap; Contracted Capacity Range: The Contracted Capacity range under
this PPA is the incremental capacity that is added by the Project above the Excluded Capacity, subject to a
Contracted Capacity Cap equal to 102.5% of the Nominal Capability, except that GPC, in its sole discretion, may
elect to accept an offer from Generator to increase the Contracted Capacity Cap under Section A.2 (Tested
Reliable Capacity; Performance Tests) of this Exhibit A.
       For the avoidance of doubt, (i) the upper limit of the Contracted Capacity range for the Term will be the
Contracted Capacity Cap; and (ii) the Contracted Capacity does not include, and this PPA does not apply to, the
Excluded Capacity.
        2.        Tested Reliable Capacity; Performance Tests: Generator must conduct Performance Testing
of the Facility under Exhibit D (Performance Testing Procedures) to determine the capacity that will reliably and
consistently be available to deliver energy to the POI under this PPA.
       Before the Delivery Commencement Date, but no earlier than 90 Days before the Delivery
Commencement Date, Generator must establish the initial Tested Reliable Capacity of the Facility pursuant to a
Performance Test. However, if Generator cannot perform the Performance Test during the period of 90 Days due
to ambient conditions, Generator must perform the Performance Test as soon as practicable with appropriate
ambient conditions after the Delivery Commencement Date.
         Following the establishment of the initial Tested Reliable Capacity of the Facility under this PPA, each
Party will have the right to request a Performance Test to re-determine the Tested Reliable Capacity to be
performed during the period from March 15 to April 15 of each Annual Period upon 10 Business Days’ written
notice to the other Party, except that, upon consent by both Parties, the Performance Test may be performed
outside the period of March 15 to April 15 of each Annual Period. No Performance Test may be scheduled during
any period of Scheduled Outage, Maintenance Outage, Force Majeure Event, or during a Forced Outage. The
Tested Reliable Capacity determined as a result of an additional Performance Test will become the new Tested
Reliable Capacity.
         If a Performance Test establishes a Tested Reliable Capacity that demonstrates incremental capacity
added by the Project above the Excluded Capacity that is greater than the then-effective Contracted Capacity
Cap, Generator may offer to increase the Contracted Capacity Cap to include the entire incremental capacity
added by the Project above the Excluded Capacity as demonstrated by such Tested Reliable Capacity and GPC
will accept or reject the offer, in its sole discretion. If GPC accepts the offer, the Contracted Capacity Cap will be
reset to include the entire incremental capacity added by the Project above the Excluded Capacity as
demonstrated by the Tested Reliable Capacity resulting from the Performance Test. If GPC does not accept the
offer, the Contracted Capacity Cap will not change.
          Generator will be responsible and bear all costs and expenses to obtain and deliver fuel required for
Performance Test(s). For Performance Test(s) required to determine the initial Tested Reliable Capacity of the
Facility, GPC will receive and purchase the test energy at the Test Energy Price. For Performance Test(s) not
required to determine the initial Tested Reliable Capacity and performed after the Commercial Operation Date,
GPC will receive and purchase the test energy at the Energy Price.
         3.       Designated Capacity: Unless Generator designates a lesser Designated Capacity as set forth
below in this Section A.3 (Designated Capacity), the “Designated Capacity” will be deemed to be the amount
equal to the Tested Reliable Capacity minus the Excluded Capacity, except that notwithstanding anything in this
PPA to the contrary, the Designated Capacity will not exceed the Contracted Capacity Cap or be less than 92%
of the Nominal Capability. If the Tested Reliable Capacity under a Performance Test demonstrates incremental
capacity added by the Project above the Excluded Capacity that is greater than the then-effective Contracted
Capacity Cap and Generator does not offer, or GPC rejects an offer, to increase the Contracted Capacity Cap
under Section A.2 (Tested Reliable Capacity; Performance Tests) of this Exhibit A, the Designated Capacity will
be deemed to be the Contracted Capacity Cap, unless Generator designates a lesser Designated Capacity as set
forth below in this Section A.3 (Designated Capacity).
       Within 10 Business Days after establishment of the Tested Reliable Capacity through a Performance
Test, Generator may elect by written notice to GPC to designate a Designated Capacity that is less than the

Capacity will not exceed the Contracted Capacity Cap and (ii) if Generator does not so designate a Designated

B.       Calculation of Monthly Availability Percentage:
         The following formula is applicable to the calculation of the MAP for a Month:
         MAP = (MDE – Monthly Excess Energy) / (Designated Capacity x MH)
         Where:
         Monthly Delivered Energy (MDE) – Has the meaning assigned in Exhibit B (Energy Payment
         Calculation).
         Monthly Excess Energy – Has the meaning assigned in Exhibit B (Energy Payment Calculation).
         Monthly Hours (MH) = the total number of hours in the Month, minus (i) any hours in the Month that the
         Facility is Unavailable as a result of any Scheduled Outages or Maintenance Outages; (ii) hours of Facility
         ramping; (iii) any hours in the Month that the Facility is Unavailable as a result of a Force Majeure Event
         declared by Generator under Part 16; and (iv) any hours in the Month that the Facility is Unavailable if the
         Unavailability is directly caused by the acts or omissions of GPC.
         An example calculation for MAP is shown in Exhibit H (Map Calculation Example).

                           EXHIBIT B – ENERGY PAYMENT CALCULATION


The Monthly Energy Payment (“MEP”) will be calculated as follows:
MEP = [(MDE - Monthly Excess Energy) * Energy Price] + ∑ [(EE * Excess Energy Price)Hour_1 …( EE * Excess
Energy Price)Hour_N] – FQFS Price Reduction
Where:
Delivered Energy (DE) = the amount of energy delivered from the Facility under this PPA each hour to the POI in
MWh. For the avoidance of doubt, Delivered Energy may include Excess Energy and does not include any energy
produced by the Facility that corresponds to the Excluded Capacity.
Monthly Delivered Energy (MDE) = ∑ (DEHour_1 … DEHour_N)
Excess Energy (EE) = the amount of Delivered Energy each hour in excess of the Designated Capacity.
Monthly Excess Energy = ∑ (EEHour_1 … EEHour_N)
Energy Price = $ REDACTED/MWh in the first Annual Period during the Term, escalating at REDACTED% on
each 12-month anniversary of the Delivery Commencement Date afterwards, as set forth in the table below.
FQFS Price Reduction = Any Future Qualifying Federal Support Amount received in the preceding tax year divided
by 12 Monthly Energy Payments. If the FQFS Price Reduction results in a negative Monthly Energy Payment
amount, the Monthly Energy Payment shall be zero dollars and any remaining Future Qualifying Federal Support
Amount shall be recovered in the following calendar year until all the portion of the Future Qualifying Federal
Support received by the Facility that GPC is entitled to receive has resulted in reductions to the Monthly Energy
Price.

                                                Energy Price
                               Annual Period during
                                                             ($/MWh)
                                      Term
                                        1                    REDACTED
                                        2                    REDACTED
                                        3                    REDACTED
                                        4                    REDACTED
                                        5                    REDACTED
                                        6                    REDACTED
                                        7                    REDACTED
                                        8                    REDACTED
                                        9                    REDACTED
                                       10                    REDACTED


Excess Energy Price = AIER x 0.90.
Examples:
If the Excluded Capacity is 40 MW, the Designated Capacity is 10 MW, and the Facility is delivering 53 MW in
any given hour, 10 MW will be paid for at the Energy Price, and 3 MW (53-40-10) will be paid for at the Excess
Energy Price.

If the Facility is delivering 35 MW in any given hour, all 35 MW will be Excluded Capacity and no energy will be
deemed delivered under this PPA.

If the Facility is delivering 42 MW in any given hour, 40 MW will be Excluded Capacity, and 2 MW will be paid for
at the Energy Price.

in the Generator’s ordinary course of business to obtain such Future Qualifying Federal Support), and therefore
the Future Qualifying Federal Support Amount is 6 million dollars, then the Monthly Energy Payment will be

                         EXHIBIT D – PERFORMANCE TESTING PROCEDURES


1. Objective.

The purpose of this Exhibit D is to provide an agreed upon method for the determination of Excluded Capacity,
Tested Reliable Capacity, and Designated Capacity of the Facility pursuant to Section 10.1. It is understood and
acknowledged that the Performance Tests will be performed pursuant to this Exhibit D: (i) prior to modification of
the Facility by the Project pursuant to Section 10.1.1, to demonstrate the Excluded Capacity of 22.5 MW for Flint
River Mill, attributed to the Pre-Existing Contract, and to provide a basis for the Parties to execute the Excluded
Capacity acknowledgment included as Attachment 1 to Exhibit B of this PPA; (ii) after modification of the Facility
by the Project, to establish the Tested Reliable Capacity and Designated Capacity of the Facility pursuant to
Section 10.1.2 and Exhibit A of this PPA; and (iii) to re-determine the Tested Reliable Capacity and Designated
Capacity pursuant to Sections A.2 and A.3, respectively, of Exhibit A of this PPA.
2. Operating Conditions.

During Performance Tests, the Facility will be operated within the normal design limits, consistent with continuous
operation, in compliance with all permit requirements, in accordance with Prudent Industry Practices, and
consistent with Generator’s reasonable operating procedures and standards (such operating procedures to be
delivered to and agreed upon by GPC prior to the Performance Test), as confirmed by available unit operating
data. The Facility will be operated with routine control set points at normal full load conditions for the duration of
the test conditions, which may include, but not be limited to, blowdown flows, makeup flows, steam turbine
extractions, station service, safety margins, and all auxiliary systems will be operated in a routine mode as
appropriate for the actual ambient conditions existing and using the Generator’s reasonable operating procedures
and standards during the test period.

3. Testing.

On the date of a Performance Test, the Facility will be brought to normal full load output capacity and operated in
a consistent and safe manner throughout the test period. The test will be scheduled between the weekday hours
of 11:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. local time. During the test period, data will be collected for a minimum of four (4) hours
at normal full load output capability. Data will be collected at least once every 10 minutes during four consecutive
one hour test runs. If the results of one test run vary by more than 0.5% from the average of all test runs, then
the reason for the discrepancy will be investigated and resolved, or the test run will be discarded. The results of
all valid test runs will then be averaged. Four consecutive one hour test runs with none of the test runs deviating
by more than 0.5% from the average of the four test runs will constitute a “Performance Test.” To the extent the
Facility experiences difficulty or unreliability during any test or its historical operating records show difficulty or
unreliability during testing of the Facility, GPC may request that Generator perform additional testing of the Facility
at Generator’s expense in order to demonstrate to GPC’s reasonable satisfaction the reliability of the Facility.

All Performance Tests will be performed using existing installed plant instrumentation. However, GPC has the
right to request calibration certification or validation by American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME)
performance test code quality instruments of key unit controls and performance data inputs. Instruments and data
points that must be operational and in good working order during all Performance Tests include: net unit electrical
output, generator power factor, station service power, steam turbine throttle temperature and pressure, steam
turbine extraction flow, ambient dry bulb temperature, ambient relative humidity, and any other parameters used
in the correction of measured output to reference conditions. All Performance Tests activities will be conducted
by, or under the supervision of, Generator and its contractors. GPC will have the right to have a representative
present to witness all Performance Tests. To request a Performance Test, each Party will provide the notice
required under Exhibit A of this PPA.

Actual net output of the Facility will be metered with the Metering System. No commercial test tolerances or
measurement uncertainties will be applied to test results.


PPA (Biomass Addition)                                Page 55 of 74

FINAL APPROVED                                                                               2023 BIOMASS RFP
[DATE]                                                                                  BIOMASS ADDITION PPA
                                                                                           PUBLIC DISCLOSURE

4. Reduction of Data.

Actual tested capacity during each test run will be adjusted to the Reference Conditions, using correction curves
standard in the industry for similarly situated biomass generators provided by Generator or its engineer in
accordance with the following equation:

Maximum Dependable Capacity = Actual Net Output x Fwetblb x Fpf

where,

Actual Net Output = Average net Facility output delivered to the GPC interface measured during the test
conducted at normal full load.

Fwetblb = correction factor for dry bulb temperature and relative humidity from actual conditions to Reference
Conditions.

Note: This correction is necessary to correct unit output for changes in cooling tower performance and its effect
on condenser pressure.

Fpf = correction for variations in power factor from actual test conditions to Reference Conditions.

Tested Reliable Capacity = Average of Maximum Dependable Capability from all valid test runs.

5. Excluded Capacity.

Following the Facility completing the testing requirements set forth in paragraph 3 above prior to modification of
the Facility by the Project, and furthermore demonstrating that the Facility can generate at least 22.5 MW for Flint
River mill of energy and associated heat requirements for a minimum of four (4) hours, then (i) the Seller shall be
deemed to have satisfied the performance requirements for the initial Performance Test set forth in this Exhibit D,
(ii) the Excluded Capacity shall be deemed to be 22.5 MW for Flint River mill, and (iii) the Parties shall execute
Attachment 1 to Exhibit B confirming that, for purposes of this PPA, Excluded Capacity shall be 22.5 MW for Flint
River mill).

                             EXHIBIT E – FACILITY DESCRIPTION AND SITE

International Paper presently owns and operates a 43.75 MW General Electric steam turbine generator, a 28 MW
General Electric steam turbine generator, and two boilers at the Flint River Mill (Oglethorpe, Georgia).

The original turbine generator is identified as TG1. It is an extraction and backpressure steam turbine that passes
steam to meet the demand of the mill’s 175# and 50# steam headers.

TG1 is supplied with steam from two boilers. The #1 Chemical Recovery Boiler burns black liquor from the pulping
process as its primary fuel and natural gas and #2 fuel oil as its supplementary fuel. The #1 Power Boiler burns
wood waste as the primary fuel and natural gas and #2 fuel oil as its supplementary fuel.

The second steam turbine generator, referred to as TG2, is a condensing steam turbine generator with a presently
rated capacity of 28 MW. It is equipped with dedicated steam supply lines to the inlet of the condensing turbine.
The capacity in MW is based on total steam flow capacity.

TG2 is co-located at the Flint River Pulp Manufacturing Mill with TG1. TG1 is self-certified as a qualifying
cogeneration facility. TG2, a condensing steam turbine, is self-certified as a small power production facility in the
Commission's docket rather than a cogeneration facility. Steam provided to TG2 is generated by two biomass
boilers on the site. One biomass boiler - referred to as a pulping liquor chemical recovery furnace - uses spent
pulping liquor as fuel. A second biomass boiler on the site - referred to as a hogged fuel boiler or a bark boiler -
uses wood bark and other wood residuals for fuel. Both biomass boilers have associated equipment for handling
fuel and ash and controlling emissions. Both boilers generate 900 psi steam at 900 deg. F. and contribute steam
to a common steam header. Both include standard steam generating equipment, e.g., air systems, superheaters,
generating banks, steam drums, etc. TG2 is located less than a mile from TG1 at International Paper’s Flint River
Mill site.

The Facility that will generate the 4.3MWs Nominal Capacity under this Biomass Power Purchase Agreement
will come primarily from a Project on TG2. TG2 will be modified to increase its current generation capacity to
approximately 35 MWs, which includes new buckets, nozzles, diaphragms, V1 modifications and HP&LP shaft
seal packing rings. Ancillary improvements on the ash removal system will occur as well, including new
hoppers, discharges, rotary lock feeders and dump valve assemblies.

The Site is defined as:
The land, rights-of-way, and related equipment and facilities of the International Paper- Flint River Mill electric
generating plant known as International Paper- Flint River Mill located in Macon County, GA at 2449 Stagecoach
Road.

                                       EXHIBIT G – FORM OF GUARANTY


This Guaranty Agreement (“Guaranty”), dated and effective as of ___________, 20__, is made and entered into
by __________________ (“Guarantor”) in favor of Georgia Power Company (“Beneficiary”).
         •     Beneficiary and ____________________ (“Company”), [a subsidiary of Guarantor], have entered
               into that certain Power Purchase Agreement for Biomass Generation dated as of ____________,
               2024 (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, “PPA”);
         •     Beneficiary has required, as an inducement to its entry into the PPA, that Guarantor deliver to
               Beneficiary this Guaranty or other Eligible Collateral as and when required under the PPA;
         •     Guarantor qualifies as a Generator Guarantor under the PPA and this Guaranty qualifies as Eligible
               Collateral under the PPA; and
         •     Guarantor will derive substantial direct and indirect benefit from the transactions contemplated by the
               PPA.
To induce Beneficiary to enter into the PPA and to perform its obligations under this Guaranty, and for and in
consideration of the foregoing premises, the mutual agreements contained in this Guaranty, and other good and
valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, Guarantor agrees as follows:

                                               ARTICLE 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1     Definitions. Unless otherwise defined in this Guaranty, capitalized terms have the meanings specified or
referred to in the PPA.

                                               ARTICLE 2 - GUARANTY
2.1     Guaranty. Guarantor unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees to Beneficiary, and its successors and
assigns, the prompt and full payment of any and all obligations of the Company to Beneficiary when due, whether
by acceleration or otherwise, with the interest as may accrue thereon, under the PPA or under any other
documents or instruments now or hereafter evidencing, securing, or otherwise relating to the PPA (the
“Guaranteed Obligations”); provided, however, that Guarantor’s liability under this Guaranty will in no event
exceed the aggregate amount of Eligible Collateral required to be provided by Generator (or Generator
Performance Security) under Part 7 (Performance Security) of the PPA (plus costs of enforcement of this Guaranty
as provided in Section 4.4 (Expenses) of this Guaranty), as the case may be. Guarantor will immediately pay for
any obligation of the Company upon demand by Beneficiary.

                   This Guaranty constitutes a guarantee of payment and not of collection. The obligations of
                   Guarantor under this Guaranty are several from the Company or any other person and are primary
                   obligations concerning which Guarantor is the principal obligor. The liability of Guarantor under
                   this Guaranty will be direct and immediate and not conditional or contingent upon the pursuit of
                   any remedies against the Company or any other person, nor against securities or liens available
                   to Beneficiary, its successors or assigns. The liability of Guarantor under this Guaranty will

                                Guaranteed Obligations, or any compromise, settlement, release, or
                                termination of any of the Guaranteed Obligations;
                         (ii)   any change, restructuring, or termination of the corporate structure or
                                existence of the Company or any of its subsidiaries, including any disposal by

                                    EXHIBIT H – MAP CALCULATION EXAMPLE2

Example #1:
Facts: Assume the Facility has a Designated Capacity of 6 MWh and delivers 10 MWh of Delivered Energy each
hour for a duration of one month (30 days).
Calculation:
Monthly Delivered Energy (MDE) = 7,200 MW
Monthly Excess Energy = MH x (Excess Energy per hour) = 720 x 4 = 2,880
Designated Capacity = 6 MW
Monthly Hours (MH) = 720
MAP = ( MDE – Monthly Excess Energy ) / ( Designated Capacity x MH ) = ( (7,200 – 2,880) / (6 X 720) ) x 100 =
100%
Example #2:
Facts: Assume the Facility has a Designated Capacity of 10 MWh and delivers 7 MWh of Delivered Energy each
hour for a duration of one month (30 days).
Calculation:
Monthly Delivered Energy (MDE) = 5,040 MW
Monthly Excess Energy = 0
Designated Capacity = 10 MW
Monthly Hours (MH) = 720
MAP = ( MDE – Monthly Excess Energy ) / (Designated Capacity x MH) = ( (5,040 – 0) / (10 X 720) ) x 100 =
70.00%
Example #3:
Facts: Assume the Facility has a Designated Capacity of 10 MWh and delivers 10 MWh in Delivered Energy each
hour for 23 days in one month (30 days). For the remaining 7 days in the month, the Facility is Unavailable as a
result of a Scheduled Outage or Maintenance Outage.
Calculation:
Monthly Delivered Energy (MDE) = 5,520 MW
Monthly Excess Energy = 0
Designated Capacity = 10 MW
Total number of hours Facility is unavailable due to Scheduled Outage = 168
Total number of hours in the month = 720
Monthly Hours (MH) = 720 – 168 = 552 hours
MAP = ( MDE – Monthly Excess Energy ) / (Designated Capacity x MH) = ( (5,520 – 0) / (10 X 552) ) x 100 =
100%


2 Note: “Delivered Energy” does not include any energy provided by the Facility corresponding to the Excluded Capacity.

===== DKT 56765 FCR-27 STF-JKA-1-PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/STF-JKA-1-22.docx =====


STF-JKA-1-22

Question: 

Please provide daily stack MRFC dispatch prices ($/MWH) for all Southern Company Service’s units included in the Company’s Aurora forecast analysis. Please show the calculation of all components used to derive the MRFC costs. Please provide the information electronically, preferably in Excel format with all formulas intact.

Response:

Dispatch prices ($/MWH) are defined in Aurora as a “Variable cost of the resource for the current hour as used in the dispatch logic”. This equates to the sum of fuel costs ($/MWH), variable operating and maintenance (VOM) costs ($/MWH), fuel handling costs ($/MWH), and emissions costs ($/MWh), all multiplied by a unit-specific bid factor (transmission penalty factor). These cost components vary primarily with fuel prices and VOM, which are modeled as monthly timeseries inputs over the simulation period. Accordingly, the average monthly dispatch price is provided in STF‑JKA‑1‑22 Attachment.

                                    SCHEDULE OF DEFINED TERMS
This PPA uses the defined terms identified in this Schedule of Defined Terms or in the body of this
PPA and the rules of construction identified in Section 20.17 (Contract Interpretation).
ACP: See Annual Capacity Price.
Affiliate: For any specific Person, any other Person directly or indirectly controlling or controlled by or under
common control with that Person. For purposes of this definition, “control” when used regarding any entity
means the power to direct the management and policies of the entity, directly or indirectly, whether through
the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise. For purposes of this PPA, it is assumed that a
Person directly or indirectly owning 50% or more of the outstanding stock or other equity interest of another
Person has “control” of that Person. The terms “controlling” and “controlled” have meanings correlative to
“control.”
After-Tax Basis: Regarding any payment received or deemed to have been received by any Person, the
amount of the payment (i.e., the base payment) supplemented by a further payment (i.e., the additional
payment) to that Person so that the sum of the base payment plus the additional payment will, after
deduction of the amount of all Taxes required to be paid by the Person regarding the receipt or accrual of
the base payment and the additional payment (taking into account any credits or deductions arising from
the underlying loss, the base payment and the additional payment and the timing of the additional payment),
be equal to the amount required to be received. The calculations will be made on the basis of the
assumption that the recipient is subject to U.S. federal income taxation at the highest applicable statutory
rate applicable to corporations for the relevant period or periods and is subject to state income taxation at
the highest applicable statutory rates applicable to corporations in the relevant jurisdiction for the relevant
period or periods.
AGC: See Automatic Generation Control.
AGC Performance Requirements: The AGC performance requirements stated in Part 3 (AGC
Performance Metrics and Requirements) of Exhibit C (Monthly Capacity Payments; Monthly Capacity
Reductions; AGC Performance Metrics and Requirements).
AGC Plan: As defined in Section 10.9 (AGC Performance Requirements).
AGC Setpoint: A value (MW) that will range from the Operating Low Limit to the Operating High Limit.
AGC Setpoint Response Performance Metric: As defined in Section 3.2.2 (AGC Setpoint Response
Performance Requirement) of Exhibit C (Monthly Capacity Payments; Monthly Capacity Reductions; AGC
Performance Metrics and Requirements).
AGC Setpoint Response Performance Requirement: As defined in Section 3.2.2 (AGC Setpoint
Response Performance Requirement) of Exhibit C (Monthly Capacity Payments; Monthly Capacity
Reductions; AGC Performance Metrics and Requirements).
AGC Status: As defined in Section 3.2.1 (AGC Status Performance Requirement) of Exhibit C (Monthly
Capacity Payments; Monthly Capacity Reductions; AGC Performance Metrics and Requirements).
AGC Status Performance Metric: As defined in Section 3.2.1 (AGC Status Performance Requirement) of
Exhibit C (Monthly Capacity Payments; Monthly Capacity Reductions; AGC Performance Metrics and
Requirements).
AGC Status Performance Requirement: As defined in Section 3.2.1 (AGC Status Performance

State of Charge (SOC): The amount of stored energy in the BESS in real time, which may be expressed

institution or conduct of any claim, action, or proceeding before FERC under Section 205, Section 206, or
any other portion of the Federal Power Act, or before any other Governmental Authority under any
applicable law that is intended to, or could reasonably be expected to, change PPA terms then in effect.
Without limiting the preceding sentence, but subject to the terms of this PPA, the Parties agree that the
rates for service specified in this PPA will remain in effect for the Term and will not be subject to change
through application to FERC in accordance with Section 205 or 206 of the Federal Power Act, or to any
other Governmental Authority under any provision of federal law, Georgia state or local law, or any other
applicable law, absent written agreement of the Parties.
       3.1.1. FERC Filings Waiver; Standard of Review. Each Party waives all rights to submit filings
       to FERC seeking modification or rescission of this PPA under Section 205 or 206 of the Federal
       Power Act.
                 (i)   FERC Standard of Review. In any proceeding before FERC involving this PPA, the
                 Parties will request that FERC review all aspects of this PPA under the “public interest”
                 application of the “just and reasonable” standard of review in United Gas Pipe Line Co. v.
                 Mobile Gas Service Corp., 350 U.S. 332 (1956) and Federal Power Commission v. Sierra
                 Pacific Power Co., 350 U.S. 348 (1956), each clarified by NRG Power Marketing LLC v.
                 Maine Public Utility Commission, 130 S. Ct. 693 (2010).

pursue, or cause to be pursued, comply with, and, as necessary, renew or modify all other Consents

perform its PPA obligations. Each Party agrees to assist and support the other Party, in a timely manner
and to the extent reasonably requested by either Party, in obtaining the Consents. Upon request, a Party
will provide a copy of Consents to the requesting Party.
